paras.zh: “我认识的每个人都参加了选举。没有人呆在家里，”萨苏尔说。她和她的家人正在分享穆塔巴克拼盘，这是一种甜美的巴勒斯坦分层糕点，还有来自今年收获的橄榄的新鲜压榨的橄榄油——这在巴勒斯坦日历上通常是一个欢乐的时刻，她说现在感觉苦乐参半。今年，被占领的约旦河西岸巴勒斯坦人的橄榄收成因以色列定居者的频繁袭击而受到破坏，他们试图扰乱一年中这个具有重要经济和文化意义的时期。

paras.en: Palestinian citizens of Israel, descendants of those who remained as the state of Israel was established in 1948 (when a majority of the prewar population was forcibly expelled or fled during the war) now make up about 20% of the population.
paras.zh: 以色列的巴勒斯坦公民是 1948 年以色列建国时留下的人的后裔（当时大多数战前人口在战争期间被强行驱逐或逃离），现在约占人口的 20%。

paras.en: This election, Arab-led parties received a 64% increase in votes compared to the last elections, according to the Central Elections Committee. The gains they made have stirred anger, and even fear, among many on Israel's political right, who see them as a threat to the country's Jewish character.
paras.zh: 据中央选举委员会称，这次选举中，阿拉伯人领导的政党获得的选票比上次选举增加了 64%。他们所取得的成果激起了许多以色列政治右翼人士的愤怒甚至恐惧，他们认为这些成果对该国的犹太性格构成了威胁。

paras.en: Netanyahu and his allies made the large Arab turnout a rallying cry. On election day, Netanyahu posted a video calling it an "emergency." Itamar Ben Gvir, the far-right national security minister, filmed his own appeal at the entrance to Kufr Qasim: "If you want this country to remain Jewish and Zionist … then get out and vote!"
paras.zh: 内塔尼亚胡和他的盟友以阿拉伯人的大量投票作为战斗口号。选举日当天，内塔尼亚胡发布了一段视频，称其为“紧急情况”。极右翼国家安全部长伊塔马尔·本·格维尔 (Itamar Ben Gvir) 在库夫尔·卡西姆 (Kufr Qasim) 入口处拍摄了自己的呼吁：“如果你希望这个国家继续是犹太人和犹太复国主义者……那就出去投票吧！”

paras.en: As results came in, Netanyahu's Likud party went further. It claimed Arab parties had "stolen" the election through bribery, threats and forgery, and later warned of a foreign takeover of the Knesset and the "Islamization of Israel." The party has made no evidence public. Police say they found no basis for the claims, and election officials say there was no widespread fraud. The head of the elections committee separately asked the Shin Bet security service to investigate suspected foreign funding of efforts to boost Arab turnout. But he and the attorney general say the vote was conducted properly and the results were not compromised.
paras.zh: 随着结果的公布，内塔尼亚胡领导的利库德集团走得更远。它声称阿拉伯政党通过贿赂、威胁和伪造“窃取”了选举，并随后警告外国接管以色列议会和“以色列伊斯兰化”。该党尚未公开任何证据。警方表示，他们没有发现这些说法的依据，选举官员表示，不存在普遍存在的欺诈行为。选举委员会负责人另外要求辛贝特安全部门调查涉嫌外国资助提高阿拉伯投票率的努力。但他和司法部长表示，投票进行得当，结果没有受到影响。

paras.en: The messaging by Netanyahu's bloc is widely seen as an attempt to prevent Eisenkot's center-right grouping from partnering with Arab parties — a reality that would give Eisenkot the majority he needs to form a government. But the sharp rise in anti-Arab sentiment since the Oct. 7, 2023 attacks, in which some 1,200 people were killed, has made an alliance with any Arab party potentially politically treacherous and could cause other Jewish right wing members of his bloc to split off in fury.
paras.zh: 内塔尼亚胡集团发出的信息被广泛视为试图阻止艾森科特的中右翼集团与阿拉伯政党合作——这一现实将使艾森科特获得组建政府所需的多数席位。但自 2023 年 10 月 7 日造成约 1,200 人死亡的袭击事件以来，反阿拉伯情绪急剧上升，与任何阿拉伯政党结盟都可能具有政治危险，并可能导致其集团中的其他犹太右翼成员愤怒地分裂。

paras.en: Eisenkot is not a natural ally for Arab parties either. A former military chief of staff whose son was killed fighting in Gaza, he served as an observer in Netanyahu's war cabinet early in the war. And he still cuts a hawkish figure. As a general, he is credited with formulating the "Dahiyeh doctrine," which he laid out in 2008: using "disproportionate force" against villages from which militants fire on Israel, which he called "not civilian villages" but "military bases." It is named after Beirut's southern suburbs, a Hezbollah stronghold that Israel largely decimated in heavy bombardment in 2006.
paras.zh: 艾森科特也不是阿拉伯政党的天然盟友。作为一名前军事参谋长，他的儿子在加沙战斗中丧生，他在战争初期担任内塔尼亚胡战时内阁的观察员。而且他仍然保持着鹰派的形象。作为一名将军，他因制定了“达希耶学说”而受到赞誉，他在 2008 年提出了这一学说：对武装分子向以色列开火的村庄使用“不成比例的武力”，他称这些村庄“不是平民村庄”，而是“军事基地”。它以贝鲁特南郊命名，贝鲁特南郊是真主党的据点，以色列在 2006 年的猛烈轰炸中大部分被摧毁。

paras.en: So Arab parties are divided on how to use the power they gained in this election. Ra'am, a socially conservative Islamist party, campaigned on joining a governing coalition and put a Jewish former police official second on its list. But for now the Joint List alliance that won 11 of the 19 Arab-led party seats in this election won't formally partner with Eisenkot. Its leaders have said they could back his government from the outside, but won't join it, citing Israel's ongoing war in Gaza and its occupation of the West Bank.
paras.zh: 因此，阿拉伯政党对于如何使用他们在这次选举中获得的权力存在分歧。拉姆是一个社会保守的伊斯兰政党，在竞选中主张加入执政联盟，并将一名犹太前警察官员列入其名单的第二位。但目前，在这次选举中赢得阿拉伯领导政党 19 个席位中 11 个席位的联合名单联盟不会与艾森科特正式合作。其领导人表示，他们可以从外部支持他的政府，但不会加入其中，理由是以色列在加沙正在进行的战争以及对约旦河西岸的占领。

paras.en: President Isaac Herzog has been consulting with parties over who they would support to try to form a coalition. He is expected to announce which candidate he'll give a mandate to next week, to try to form a coalition. That candidate will have 28 days and can ask for a further two-week extension. If he fails, another candidate is given only 28 days (without extension) to try to form a government. And if no one manages to form a coalition, there will be repeat elections next year.
paras.zh: 艾萨克·赫尔佐格总统一直在与各党派协商他们将支持谁来组建联合政府。预计他将在下周宣布将授权给哪位候选人，以尝试组建联盟。该候选人将有 28 天的时间，并且可以要求再延长两周。如果他失败了，另一位候选人只有 28 天（不得延期）的时间尝试组建政府。如果没有人能够组建联合政府，明年将再次举行选举。

paras.en: In Kufr Qasim, as the readings and re-enactments of the 1956 killings unfurled on stage, Mansour Shaaban said he would vote again in an instant. Aged 33, this was the first election he had voted in. But now he said it's necessary to try to stop what he called the racism and oppression of Palestinians by Israel's extreme right. "There are Israelis we eat with and live alongside," Shaaban said. But Netanyahu and Ben-Gvir and other leaders in these last years he said "are making it impossible to co-exist," he said.
paras.zh: 在库夫尔卡西姆，当 1956 年大屠杀的朗诵和重演在舞台上展开时，曼苏尔·沙班表示他将立即再次投票。 33岁的他参加了第一次选举。但现在他表示，有必要努力制止他所谓的以色列极右翼对巴勒斯坦人的种族主义和压迫。 “我们和以色列人一起吃饭、一起生活，”沙班说。但他说，内塔尼亚胡和本格维尔以及其他领导人在过去几年“正在使共存变得不可能”。

paras.en: "Even if we don't succeed to create change this time," he said, now right-wing Israeli politicians know that Palestinian citizens of the country have found their voice.
paras.zh: 他说：“即使我们这次未能成功创造变革，”现在以色列右翼政客知道该国的巴勒斯坦公民已经找到了自己的声音。

articles.title: Tiger Woods and ex-wife Elin Nordegren reunite to celebrate son Charlie's college golf commitment

paras.en: It was a family reunion for Charlie Woods on Friday, as both his father and mother, whose divorce was highly publicized, were together again to celebrate his college commitment.
paras.zh: 周五，查理·伍兹 (Charlie Woods) 举行了一次家庭聚会，他的父母（他们的离婚广为人知）再次聚在一起庆祝他的大学承诺。

paras.en: Woods, the son of 15-time major winner Tiger, announced earlier this year his commitment to play golf at Florida State University.
paras.zh: 伍兹是 15 届大满贯赛冠军泰格的儿子，今年早些时候宣布他将在佛罗里达州立大学打高尔夫球。

paras.en: The Woods family, including Tiger's ex-wife, Elin Nordegren, were on hand at Charlie's high school to celebrate.
paras.zh: 伍兹一家，包括泰格的前妻艾琳·诺德格伦，都在查理的高中庆祝。

paras.en: Tiger and Elin got divorced after the former's infidelity had been exposed.
paras.zh: 泰格和艾琳在前者的不忠行为曝光后离婚了。

paras.en: Charlie announced the commitment in February.
paras.zh: 查理在二月份宣布了这一承诺。

paras.en: "Excited to announce my commitment to play golf at Florida State University — go Noles!" he wrote.
paras.zh: “很高兴宣布我承诺在佛罗里达州立大学打高尔夫球 - 诺尔斯加油！”他写道。

paras.en: "Congratulations Charlie. I'm so proud of you on entering this next chapter of your life," Tiger commented.
paras.zh: “恭喜查理。我为你进入人生的下一个篇章感到非常自豪，”泰格评论道。

paras.en: It is a rare public appearance for Tiger, who has remained out of the spotlight most of the time since he was arrested in March.
paras.zh: 对于老虎来说，这是一次罕见的公开露面，自三月份被捕以来，他大部分时间都没有出现在聚光灯下。

paras.en: He was arrested on charges of DUI following a car crash in which police later found hydrocodone pills in his pocket. It was his second DUI in less than a decade. Woods previously told law enforcement prior to the field sobriety tests that he underwent seven back surgeries and "over 20 operations on his leg." He told law enforcement that "I take a few" prescription medications.
paras.zh: 他在一场车祸后因酒后驾车被捕，警方后来在他的口袋里发现了氢可酮药片。这是他不到十年内第二次酒后驾车。伍兹此前在现场清醒测试之前告诉执法部门，他接受了七次背部手术和“超过 20 次腿部手术”。他告诉执法部门，“我服用了一些”处方药。

paras.en: According to an arrest affidavit obtained by Fox News Digital, deputies with the Martin County Sheriff’s Office reported observing several signs of impairment at the scene, noting that the golf legend was "sweating profusely" and that his movements appeared "lethargic and slow." Law enforcement proceeded to perform field sobriety tests because of their suspicions. Woods was instructed to remove his eyeglasses, and the deputy conducting the tests stated that his eyes appeared to be "bloodshot and glassy" and "extremely dilated."
paras.zh: 根据福克斯新闻数字频道获得的一份逮捕证词，马丁县治安官办公室的代表报告称，他们在现场观察到了一些受伤的迹象，并指出这位高尔夫传奇人物“大汗淋漓”，动作显得“昏昏欲睡、缓慢”。出于怀疑，执法部门开始进行现场清醒测试。伍兹被指示摘下眼镜，负责测试的副手表示，他的眼睛似乎“充血且呆滞”并且“极度扩张”。

paras.en: Shortly after the arrest, Woods announced he was seeking treatment.
paras.zh: 被捕后不久，伍兹宣布他正在寻求治疗。

paras.en: Nordegren was reportedly "concerned" after the legendary golfer’s arrest.
paras.zh: 据报道，诺德格伦在这位传奇高尔夫球手被捕后感到“担忧”。

paras.en: Tiger's return to the golf course remains to be determined — he has not played since the 2024 Open Championship. When he was arrested in March, he said he was "hoping to" play in April's Masters, but he ultimately missed the entire 2026 season.
paras.zh: 老虎是否重返高尔夫球场仍有待确定——他自 2024 年公开赛以来就没有参加过比赛。当他在 3 月份被捕时，他表示“希望”参加 4 月份的大师赛，但他最终错过了整个 2026 年赛季。

articles.title: Rams safety Quentin Lake apologizes to Justin Herbert for 'deli meat' comment, even though he has a point

paras.en: One of the weird things about modern sports is that current athletes will gladly hop on podcasts. Of course, that sometimes makes things awkward, as was the case for Rams safety Quentin Lake.
paras.zh: 现代体育运动的奇怪之处之一是，当前的运动员会很乐意跳上播客。当然，这有时会让事情变得尴尬，公羊队安全卫昆汀·莱克的情况就是如此。

paras.en: Lake went on the "St. Brown Podcast" hosted by Lions receiver Amon-Ra St. Brown and his brother Equanimeous St. Brown.
paras.zh: 莱克参加了由狮子队接球手阿蒙-拉·圣·布朗和他的兄弟埃奎尼米乌斯·圣·布朗主持的“圣布朗播客”。

paras.en: On the show, Lake talked about an interception he made on Sunday against the Los Angeles Chargers and was not complimentary of quarterback Justin Herbert's play.
paras.zh: 在节目中，莱克谈到了他周日对阵洛杉矶闪电队的一次拦截，并没有赞扬四分卫贾斯汀·赫伯特的表现。

paras.en: "He was throwing deli meat out there," Lake said on the St. Brown Podcast. "He's seeing ghosts. I don't know what's going on, but we knew we were gonna get a couple. At least one."
paras.zh: “他把熟食肉扔在那里，”莱克在圣布朗播客上说。 “他看到了鬼魂。我不知道发生了什么，但我们知道我们会遇到两个。至少一个。”

paras.en: Alright, just a couple of guys being dudes, talking smack.
paras.zh: 好吧，只是几个家伙，正在说着脏话。

paras.en: Also, have you seen the 0-7 Chargers this year? "Throwing deli meat" might be a compliment compared to what they've done at times during the season. Seeing ghosts would actually be a welcome explanation.
paras.zh: 还有，今年的0-7充电器你看过吗？与他们在这个季节有时所做的事情相比，“扔熟食肉”可能是一种赞美。看到鬼魂实际上是一个受欢迎的解释。

paras.en: So, no harm, no foul. Nothing wrong with a little smack talk in the NFL.
paras.zh: 所以，没有伤害，没有犯规。在美国国家橄榄球联盟（NFL）中，说一些谩骂的话并没有什么错。

paras.en: According to The Los Angeles Times, Lake sent an apology to Herbert over text message, but had not heard back.
paras.zh: 据《洛杉矶时报》报道，莱克通过短信向赫伯特致歉，但尚未收到回复。

paras.en: "I don’t know if he read it," Lake said. "He probably says, 'I don’t care about it anymore. I’m not trying to see this. It doesn’t matter. You said what you said.' But at the same time I … felt like it was right for me to at least say, 'Hey, man, I didn’t mean it in any disrespectful way.'"
paras.zh: “我不知道他是否读过，”莱克说。 “他可能会说，‘我不再关心它了。我不想看到这个。没关系。你说了你说的。’但与此同时，我……觉得我至少应该说，‘嘿，伙计，我并没有任何不尊重的意思。’”

paras.en: Come on, Justin: He meant you were throwing deli meat in the most respectful way imaginable!
paras.zh: 来吧，贾斯汀：他的意思是你正在以可以想象到的最尊重的方式扔熟食肉！

paras.en: Good on Lake for apologizing. But let's be honest, there's nothing wrong with a little off-field smack talk.
paras.zh: 湖上的道歉很好。但说实话，场外的一些谩骂并没有什么问题。

paras.en: And if Herbert is offended by his passes being compared to someone flinging some Boar's Head around, then maybe work on not leading the league with ten interceptions.
paras.zh: 如果赫伯特因为他的传球被比作有人扔野猪头而感到生气，那么也许会努力不以十次拦截领先联盟。

paras.en: That should be the rule: as long as you're at the top of the picks-thrown leaderboard, everyone gets to say you're throwing deli meat.
paras.zh: 这应该是规则：只要你在投出的选秀排行榜上名列前茅，每个人都会说你投出了熟食肉。

articles.title: DeSantis blasts Washington Post over report he's preparing 2028 presidential bid

paras.en: Florida Gov. Ron DeSantis fired back Friday at a report that he is preparing another White House bid in 2028, accusing The Washington Post of fabricating claims that he has started reaching out to political consultants about a potential campaign.
paras.zh: 佛罗里达州州长罗恩·德桑蒂斯周五对有关他正在准备 2028 年再次入主白宫的报道进行了反击，指责《华盛顿邮报》捏造了他已开始就潜在竞选活动与政治顾问接触的说法。

paras.en: "The Washington Post is fabricating this out of whole cloth," DeSantis wrote on X. "I have not reached out to anybody about running for anything."
paras.zh: 德桑蒂斯在 X 上写道：“《华盛顿邮报》完全捏造了这一点。”“我还没有与任何人接触过竞选任何事情。”

paras.en: "Just another pathetic attempt to garner clicks. Using anonymous sources of course!" he added.
paras.zh: “这只是另一种获取点击量的可悲尝试。当然是使用匿名来源！”他补充道。

paras.en: The Post reported Friday, citing three people briefed on his plans, that DeSantis was preparing to seek the Republican presidential nomination in 2028.
paras.zh: 《华盛顿邮报》周五援引三名知情人士的话说，德桑蒂斯正准备在 2028 年寻求共和党总统提名。

paras.en: The newspaper reported that DeSantis, who unsuccessfully ran for president in 2024 and is term-limited after 2026, had already reached out to at least one national political consultant about working on a prospective campaign.
paras.zh: 该报报道称，德桑蒂斯在 2024 年竞选总统失败，并在 2026 年之后任期有限，他已经与至少一位国家政治顾问联系，商讨未来的竞选活动。

paras.en: A federal super PAC tied to DeSantis also sent out a fundraising text earlier this week, The Post reported.
paras.zh: 据《华盛顿邮报》报道，与德桑蒂斯相关的联邦超级政治行动委员会本周早些时候也发出了筹款短信。

paras.en: DeSantis continued pushing back against the report in exchanges with social media users.
paras.zh: 德桑蒂斯在与社交媒体用户的交流中继续反驳该报告。

paras.en: When one user expressed hope that The Post's reporting was accurate, the governor replied that he was "sorry to disappoint."
paras.zh: 当一名用户表示希望《华盛顿邮报》的报道准确时，州长回答说他“很抱歉让大家失望了”。

paras.en: DeSantis also responded to another user who suggested political consultants may have been using his name to attract attention.
paras.zh: 德桑蒂斯还回应了另一位用户的说法，该用户表示政治顾问可能一直在使用他的名字来吸引注意力。

paras.en: "Probably the case. But maybe just made up by WaPo," he wrote.
paras.zh: “可能是这样。但也许只是华盛顿邮报编造的，”他写道。

paras.en: Speculation surrounding DeSantis' political future comes just days after Republicans suffered sweeping defeats in the midterm elections, losing control of both chambers of Congress and several traditionally Republican strongholds.
paras.zh: 就在几天前，共和党在中期选举中惨败，失去了对国会两院和几个共和党传统据点的控制权，围绕德桑蒂斯政治未来的猜测出现。

paras.en: The Sunshine State, however, remained a bright spot for the GOP, with Republican Byron Donalds winning the governor's race.
paras.zh: 然而，阳光之州仍然是共和党的亮点，共和党人拜伦·唐纳德赢得了州长竞选。

paras.en: "This is close to an extinction-level event for Republicans," DeSantis said Wednesday, warning that among the nation's 10 most populous states, Florida would be the only one with Republican control of its government.
paras.zh: 德桑蒂斯周三表示：“这对共和党来说几乎是一场灭绝级别的事件。”他警告说，在全国人口最多的 10 个州中，佛罗里达州将是唯一一个由共和党控制其政府的州。

paras.en: DeSantis previously sought the 2024 Republican presidential nomination but suspended his campaign in January 2024 after the Iowa caucuses and endorsed Donald Trump.
paras.zh: 德桑蒂斯此前曾寻求 2024 年共和党总统提名，但在爱荷华州党团会议后于 2024 年 1 月暂停竞选活动，转而支持唐纳德·特朗普。

paras.en: The governor, who will leave office in January, has previously left open the possibility of another presidential campaign.
paras.zh: 这位将于一月卸任的州长此前曾表示有可能再次竞选总统。

paras.en: Fox News Digital has reached out to DeSantis' office and The Washington Post for comment.
paras.zh: 福克斯新闻数字频道已联系德桑蒂斯办公室和《华盛顿邮报》征求意见。

paras.en: Fox News Digital's Charles Creitz contributed to this report.
paras.zh: 福克斯新闻数字频道的查尔斯·克雷茨 (Charles Creitz) 对本报告做出了贡献。

articles.title: US carries out another round of ‘minor’ strikes on Iran, Trump says
articles.author: Guardian staff and agencies

paras.en: Donald Trump has said the US military on Friday carried out a new round of limited strikes on Iran, targeting an air defence system, describing the action as “minor.”
paras.zh: 唐纳德·特朗普表示，美国军方周五对伊朗进行了新一轮有限打击，目标是防空系统，并称此次行动“规模较小”。

paras.en: Iranian state media reported the sound of two explosions in the Suza area of Qeshm Island, which is in the strait of Hormuz, the crucial waterway for oil shipments that has been disrupted since the beginning of the US war on Iran in February.
paras.zh: 伊朗官方媒体报道了格什姆岛苏扎地区发生的两起爆炸声，该地区位于霍尔木兹海峡，自二月份美国对伊朗战争开始以来，霍尔木兹海峡是石油运输的重要航道，该航道一直受到干扰。

paras.en: In an exchange with reporters on Friday, Trump said “they built a little bit of an anti-aircraft device and we knocked it out in about 15 minutes, maybe five”.
paras.zh: 特朗普周五在与记者交流时表示，“他们建造了一些防空装置，我们在大约 15 分钟（也许是 5 分钟）内将其摧毁”。

paras.en: The US military had previously reported carrying out what it described as “defensive” strikes on Monday, when explosions were heard on the islands of Qeshm and Hengam and in the nearby mainland area of Bandar Abbas.
paras.zh: 美国军方此前曾报告称，周一进行了所谓的“防御性”打击，当时格什姆岛、恒加姆岛以及附近的阿巴斯港大陆地区都听到爆炸声。

paras.en: Friday’s strikes are the first since Trump’s Republican party was dealt a stunning repudiation in Tuesday’s midterm elections in the US.
paras.zh: 周五的罢工是自特朗普所在的共和党在周二美国中期选举中遭到令人震惊的拒绝以来的首次罢工。

paras.en: The electoral setback was stoked in part by voter dissatisfaction with Trump’s execution of the Iran war and elevated fuel prices – a byproduct of the war that has affected nearly every part of the global economy.
paras.zh: 选举受挫的部分原因是选民对特朗普执行伊朗战争和油价上涨感到不满——这是战争的副产品，几乎影响了全球经济的各个领域。

paras.en: In the days since, Trump has vacillated between threatening to “destroy” Iran and suggesting a resolution to the war is near.
paras.zh: 此后的几天里，特朗普在威胁“摧毁”伊朗和暗示战争即将得到解决之间犹豫不决。

paras.en: Differences with Iran about its nuclear program remain the thorniest issue and one that Trump insists must be resolved as part of any deal meant to end the war.
paras.zh: 与伊朗在核计划上的分歧仍然是最棘手的问题，特朗普坚持认为，这一问题必须作为任何旨在结束战争的协议的一部分得到解决。

paras.en: US Central Command, which oversees US military operations in the Middle East, announced in a post on X late Friday that the US was offering “a reward of up to $20m and possible relocation for information about Iran’s nuclear program, including its facilities, equipment, and associated personnel, such as those in the scientific community, or the movement of any of the above”.
paras.zh: 负责监督美国在中东军事行动的美国中央司令部周五晚间在一篇帖子中宣布，美国将“悬赏高达 2000 万美元，并可能对有关伊朗核计划的信息进行重新安置，包括其设施、设备和相关人员，例如科学界的人员，或上述任何人员的动向”。

paras.en: The post included a link to the state department’s Rewards for Justice program.
paras.zh: 该帖子包含国务院正义奖励计划的链接。

paras.en: Trump noted earlier Friday in an exchange with reporters that mediators’ discussions with Iran continue.
paras.zh: 特朗普周五早些时候在与记者的交流中指出，调解人与伊朗的讨论仍在继续。

paras.en: “We are talking to Iran. We have been,” said Trump.
paras.zh: “我们正在与伊朗对话。我们一直在对话，”特朗普说。

paras.en: A flurry of diplomatic phone calls in recent days between leaders in the Gulf and beyond has been aimed at easing tensions in the region. Concerns have mounted over the possibility that Trump could still order the US military to carry out new strikes against Iran.
paras.zh: 最近几天，海湾地区及其他地区领导人之间进行了一系列外交通话，旨在缓解该地区的紧张局势。人们越来越担心特朗普仍可能命令美军对伊朗进行新的打击。

paras.en: US defense secretary Pete Hegseth spoke on Friday with his Qatari counterpart, Sheikh Saoud bin Abdulrahman Al Thani, about developments, according to the Qatari government. Qatar has been mediating between the US and Iran to end the war.
paras.zh: 据卡塔尔政府称，美国国防部长皮特·赫格斯周五与卡塔尔国防部长谢赫·萨乌德·本·阿卜杜拉赫曼·阿勒萨尼就事态发展进行了交谈。卡塔尔一直在美国和伊朗之间进行调解，以结束战争。

paras.en: The Qatari government announced the call between the countries’ defence officials after confirming earlier that Trump and Qatar’s emir had a separate call to discuss efforts to de-escalate tensions.
paras.zh: 卡塔尔政府早些时候确认特朗普和卡塔尔埃米尔单独通话，讨论缓和紧张局势的努力，随后宣布了两国国防官员之间的通话。

paras.en: The telephone call between Trump and Qatar’s Emir Sheikh Tamim bin Hamad al Thani focused on international efforts to end tensions, according to a statement from the Qatari ruler’s media office.
paras.zh: 卡塔尔统治者媒体办公室的一份声明称，特朗普与卡塔尔埃米尔谢赫塔米姆·本·哈马德·阿勒萨尼之间的电话重点讨论了结束紧张局势的国际努力。

articles.title: What’s the point? Ten years after the Paris treaty, are climate talks getting anywhere?
articles.author: Fiona Harvey in Antalya, Turkey

paras.en: It was a curious way of conducting negotiations. Ahead of the 2025 climate summit, in the Amazonian port of Belém last year, the Brazilian hosts had taken off the table the issue that most had assumed would be at its heart: concrete plans from each country laying out exactly what they would be doing to cut their greenhouse gas emissions.
paras.zh: 这是一种奇怪的谈判方式。去年在亚马逊贝伦港举行的 2025 年气候峰会之前，巴西东道主把大多数人认为是核心问题的问题搁置一旁：每个国家都制定了具体计划，明确说明了他们将采取哪些措施来减少温室气体排放。

paras.en: Brazil was insisting, instead, that these plans – the bedrock of the Paris agreement – were the business of national governments and not up for negotiation. “In that case, it will be a very short Cop,” one seasoned global south negotiator told the Guardian shortly before, reflecting a widespread unease. “There is nothing to negotiate.”
paras.zh: 相反，巴西坚称这些计划 — — 《巴黎协定》的基石 — — 是各国政府的事，不需进行谈判。一位经验丰富的全球南方谈判代表不久前告诉《卫报》，“在这种情况下，警察的任期将非常短”，这反映出普遍的不安。 “没有什么可谈判的。”

paras.en: “They have decided that there is no appetite for negotiation, with the US out of Paris,” said another developing country diplomat. “Countries won’t engage.”
paras.zh: 另一位发展中国家外交官表示：“他们已经决定没有兴趣与美国退出巴黎进行谈判。” “各国不会参与。”

paras.en: The summit ended with a deal, although few loved it. But, as the faultlines from the Brazilian decision deepen going into this year’s summit, it is clear that the Paris agreement, and climate action around the world, has reached an impasse.
paras.zh: 峰会以一项协议结束，尽管很少有人喜欢它。但是，随着今年峰会上巴西决定的分歧加深，巴黎协定和世界各地的气候行动显然已经陷入僵局。

paras.en: And it is not just Cop insiders who are worried. For many outside the vast white air-conditioned conference halls, the question, as this year’s summit begins, will be: what is the point?
paras.zh: 担心的不仅仅是警察内部人士。对于在巨大的白色空调会议厅外的许多人来说，随着今年的峰会开始，问题将是：意义何在？

paras.en: Those same governments have pledged year after year since the Paris agreement was signed in 2015 – and entered into force a year later – to limit global heating to 1.5C above preindustrial levels. Yet temperatures for two years have exceeded that threshold, and the UN revealed a few weeks ago that its most optimistic estimate was now for about 1.7 to 1.8C of heating.
paras.zh: 自 2015 年巴黎协定签署（并于一年后生效）以来，这些政府年复一年地承诺将全球升温限制在比工业化前水平高 1.5 摄氏度的范围内。然而，两年来的气温都超过了这一阈值，联合国几周前透露，目前最乐观的估计是供暖温度约为 1.7 至 1.8 摄氏度。

paras.en: There could be no clearer evidence that the Paris agreement, on the face of it, has failed. It is impossible not to wonder whether the Cop process itself is just not fit for purpose.
paras.zh: 从表面上看，没有更明确的证据表明《巴黎协定》已经失败。我们不可能不怀疑 Cop 流程本身是否不符合其目的。

paras.en: The charge sheet against Paris is long, with the central issue being the failure to achieve its goal. Beyond that immediate failure, the negotiation processes are endlessly convoluted and cause their own problems. It took more than five years just to negotiate the Paris “rulebook” under which the treaty is interpreted and put into effect.
paras.zh: 对巴黎的指控很长，核心问题是未能实现其目标。除了立即失败之外，谈判过程也是无休无止地错综复杂，并引发了自己的问题。仅就巴黎“规则手册”的谈判就花费了五年多的时间，该《规则手册》是该条约的解释和实施的依据。

paras.en: The convention that all resolutions must pass by consensus has given bad actors free rein. Donald Trump’s allies – in Saudi Arabia, Russia, Venezuela and some other petrostates – frequently veto measures and obstruct progress.
paras.zh: 所有决议都必须以协商一致方式通过的惯例让坏人得以肆意妄为。唐纳德·特朗普的盟友——沙特阿拉伯、俄罗斯、委内瑞拉和其他一些石油国家——经常否决措施并阻碍进展。

paras.en: It took more than 30 years of negotiation since the UN framework convention on climate change was signed in 1992 for fossil fuels even to be addressed directly. This was at Cop28 in Dubai in 2023, where countries agreed for the first time to “transition away from fossil fuels” but failed to set a timeframe or any policies to back up the resolution.
paras.zh: 自1992年签署《联合国气候变化框架公约》以来，即使是直接解决化石燃料问题，也经过了30多年的谈判。这是 2023 年在迪拜举行的第 28 届缔约方会议，各国首次同意“摆脱化石燃料”，但未能设定时间表或任何支持该决议的政策。

paras.en: The US, the world’s biggest economy and responsible for about one in every eight tonnes of carbon dioxide emitted today, has withdrawn from Paris under President Trump.
paras.zh: 美国是世界上最大的经济体，今天排放的二氧化碳约占八分之一，美国已在特朗普总统的领导下退出巴黎。

paras.en: Even parts of the developed world which support the process have mostly failed to come up with convincing plans: Australia, co-host of Cop31, has set no end to fossil fuel exports; its fellow co-host Turkey plans to increase its carbon output. The UK is opening a gasfield and mulling a new oilfield, Germany has dropped its electric vehicle sales targets and scrapped a renewable heating law. Meanwhile, most rich countries are reducing their contributions to climate finance for the poor.
paras.zh: 即使是支持这一进程的部分发达国家也大多未能拿出令人信服的计划：第三十一届缔约方大会共同主办国澳大利亚并未限制化石燃料出口；其共同主办国土耳其计划增加其碳排放量。英国正在开辟一个气田并考虑建设一个新油田，德国放弃了电动汽车销售目标并废除了可再生能源供暖法。与此同时，大多数富裕国家正在减少对穷人的气候融资的贡献。

paras.en: Most of all, the slow pace of the Paris timetable might have seemed fine in 2015, when temperatures were rising at 0.2C a decade. Today, the rate of rise is 0.4C a decade and still accelerating.
paras.zh: 最重要的是，巴黎时间表的缓慢节奏在 2015 年可能看起来还不错，当时气温每十年上升 0.2 摄氏度。如今，上升速度为每十年 0.4C，并且仍在加速。

paras.en: “The structures of Cops and Paris are labyrinthine, bureaucratic, and ultimately dispiriting,” said Paul Bledsoe, a former Clinton White House climate adviser, now with the American University. “It may be time to streamline them to focus more deliberately on national emissions reduction goals.”
paras.zh: “警察和巴黎的结构是迷宫般的、官僚主义的，而且最终令人沮丧，”前克林顿白宫气候顾问、现供职于美国大学的保罗·布莱索说。 “也许是时候精简它们，更加专注于国家减排目标了。”

paras.en: As ordinary people watch these failures outside and inside the process, some are losing faith. The Paris agreement was a sensation, celebrated around the world. In the years since, the aura of Cop has faded, as meetings seem to disintegrate into arguments over wording and compromise.
paras.zh: 当普通人目睹这些过程内外的失败时，有些人正在失去信心。巴黎协定轰动一时，全世界都庆祝。从那以后的几年里，警察的光环逐渐消失，因为会议似乎分解为措辞和妥协的争论。

paras.en: “A lot of the commitments, the promises that were made, just turned out to be a bunch of hot air,” said Juan Carlos Monterrey, former climate envoy for Panama, now chief executive of the Vanglabs consultancy. “Under that measure, we have failed.”
paras.zh: 巴拿马前气候特使、现任 Vanglabs 咨询公司首席执行官胡安·卡洛斯·蒙特雷 (Juan Carlos Monterrey) 表示：“很多承诺，已经做出的承诺，最后都变成了一堆废话。” “按照这个标准，我们失败了。”

paras.en: Johan Rockström, director of the Potsdam Institute for Climate Impact Research, said: “The fact that global warming is accelerating, that we inevitably will be breaching the 1.5C limit within three to five years, that tipping points are coming closer fast, that Earth’s resilience is showing worrying signs of decline, and that we still allow ourselves to follow a global path that will take us to a catastrophic 2.6C-3C, and that this is allowed to happen within the framework of the Paris agreement, cannot be considered as anything but a global failure.”
paras.zh: 波茨坦气候影响研究所所长约翰·洛克斯特罗姆（Johan Rockström）表示：“事实上，全球变暖正在加速，我们将不可避免地在三到五年内突破1.5摄氏度的限制，临界点正在快速逼近，地球的恢复力正在显示出令人担忧的下降迹象，而且我们仍然允许自己走一条将导致灾难性的2.6摄氏度至3摄氏度的全球道路，而这在《巴黎协定》的框架内是允许发生的。协议只能被视为全球性的失败。”

paras.en: But, like most involved in international climate efforts, both refuse to concede that Paris is done for. “On the other hand,” said Rockström, “Paris is all we have. And we know that the global climate crisis can only, in the end, be solved if all countries in the world simultaneously move away from planet-damaging heat injection.”
paras.zh: 但是，就像大多数参与国际气候努力的人一样，两人都拒绝承认巴黎已经完蛋了。 “另一方面，”罗克斯特伦说，“巴黎就是我们的全部。而且我们知道，只有世界所有国家同时停止对地球造成破坏的热注入，全球气候危机最终才能得到解决。”

paras.en: Monterrey agrees. The most important fact about the Paris agreement, and the Cop process, he says, is that they exist. “Paris is our moral compass. It has told us where we should go. The speed of travel is not what it needs to be, but Paris has set the direction.”
paras.zh: 蒙特雷同意。他说，关于《巴黎协定》和《缔约方会议》程序的最重要事实是它们的存在。 “巴黎是我们的道德指南针。它告诉我们应该去哪里。旅行的速度不是我们需要的，但巴黎已经设定了方向。”

paras.en: This year’s Cop is the first to have a split presidency and host. Being held in Turkey but presided over by Australia, Cop31 is a messy compromise between two countries whose other chief point of commonality is an admiration for coal.
paras.zh: 今年的《警察》是第一次由主席和主持人分开的会议。第三十一届缔约方会议在土耳其举行，由澳大利亚主持，是两个国家之间的混乱妥协，这两个国家的另一个主要共同点是对煤炭的钦佩。

paras.en: Unexpectedly, however, the skies are a little brighter over this year’s meeting than anyone might have expected. Brazil has decisively re-elected Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva who has already overseen the biggest reductions in deforestation for decades.
paras.zh: 然而，出乎意料的是，今年会议的天空比任何人预期的都要明亮一些。巴西果断选举路易斯·伊纳西奥·卢拉·达席尔瓦连任，他已经监督了数十年来最大程度的森林砍伐减少。

paras.en: The US midterms delivered a drubbing for the right, while in Serbia and Hungary this year democracy has won out over authoritarianism. Though the far right is still on the march across much of Europe, and autocrats still rule in most of the countries with the biggest fossil fuel industries and highest emissions, the replacement or weakening of anti-climate authoritarians by pro-climate parties is a positive sign. Globally, a large majority of people support climate action.
paras.zh: 美国中期选举让右翼惨败，而今年在塞尔维亚和匈牙利，民主战胜了威权主义。尽管极右翼势力仍在欧洲大部分地区蔓延，而且独裁者仍然统治着大多数拥有最大化石燃料工业和排放量最高的国家，但支持气候政党取代或削弱反气候独裁者是一个积极的迹象。在全球范围内，绝大多数人支持气候行动。

paras.en: Action beyond the framework of Cop is marching on. After the failure of last year’s Cop30 in Brazil to provide a strong statement on phasing out fossil fuels, a group of nearly 60 countries held an alternative meeting in Colombia in April and agreed to draw up their own national roadmaps for the “transition away from fossil fuels”.
paras.zh: 超出《警察》框架的行动正在继续进行。去年在巴西举行的第 30 届缔约方会议未能就逐步淘汰化石燃料发表强有力的声明后，近 60 个国家于 4 月在哥伦比亚举行了一次替代会议，并同意制定自己的国家“摆脱化石燃料转型”路线图。

paras.en: Three major countries have so far done so: France, Germany and the Netherlands. Bledsoe wants to use this model for more side agreements on the “super pollutants” such as methane, refrigerant chemicals called HFCs, ground-level ozone, nitrous oxide and black carbon, or soot.
paras.zh: 迄今为止，三个主要国家已经这样做了：法国、德国和荷兰。布莱索希望利用这一模型就“超级污染物”达成更多附带协议，例如甲烷、称为 HFC 的制冷剂化学品、地面臭氧、一氧化二氮和黑碳或烟灰。

paras.en: Cutting methane by 40% could alone hold down temperatures by about 0.3C in the next decade, and deeper cuts beyond that could yield a 0.5C decrease by 2100.
paras.zh: 仅将甲烷排放量减少 40% 就可以在未来 10 年将气温降低约 0.3 摄氏度，超过此范围的进一步削减可能会导致到 2100 年气温下降 0.5 摄氏度。

paras.en: “Paris was never intended to do all the hard work itself,” Bledsoe said. “We need to use the G7, the G20 and other forums too, and we need to elevate the climate to the level of national security concern, and see it as an economic threat.”
paras.zh: “巴黎从来没有打算自己承担所有艰苦的工作，”布莱索说。 “我们还需要利用七国集团、二十国集团和其他论坛，我们需要将气候问题提升到国家安全担忧的水平，并将其视为经济威胁。”

paras.en: While the failures of Paris might seem obvious, its “moral compass” has also translated into greater success in the real world than many people realise.
paras.zh: 虽然巴黎的失败似乎是显而易见的，但它的“道德指南针”也在现实世界中转化为比许多人意识到的更大的成功。

paras.en: “The solar panels on my roof and the BYD Dolphin [electric car] my neighbour drives are exhibit one and exhibit two of Paris’s success,” said Claudio Angelo, of the Observatório do Clima thinktank. “Will Paris prevent overshoot of 1.5C? No way. Will it prevent 2C of warming? Unlikely. But the transformation it has triggered can’t be exaggerated.”
paras.zh: “我屋顶上的太阳能电池板和我邻居开的比亚迪海豚（电动汽车）是巴黎成功的展示之一和展示之二，”Observatório do Clima 智囊团的克劳迪奥·安杰洛（Claudio Angelo）说。 “巴黎会阻止气温上升 1.5 摄氏度吗？不可能。它会阻止升温 2 摄氏度吗？不太可能。但它引发的转变怎么夸大都不过分。”

paras.en: Perhaps the clinching argument lies in China, the world’s biggest emitter of greenhouse gases and second-largest economy.
paras.zh: 也许最关键的论点在于中国，它是世界上最大的温室气体排放国和第二大经济体。

paras.en: “China is taking multilateral climate efforts more seriously than many other countries, and certainly more seriously than it did a few years ago,” said Li Shuo, director of the China climate hub at the Asia Society Policy Institute. “The reason is simple: its economic stakes have grown enormously. If the world abandons decarbonisation, where will China sell its solar panels and electric vehicles?”
paras.zh: 亚洲协会政策研究所中国气候中心主任李硕表示：“中国比许多其他国家更认真地对待多边气候努力，当然也比几年前更认真。” “原因很简单：中国的经济利益已经大大增加。如果世界放弃脱碳，中国将在哪里出售太阳能电池板和电动汽车？”

paras.en: And, stung by high fossil fuel prices, many developing-country consumers are grasping clean technology without waiting for assistance. In Pakistan, plagued by blackouts and grid supply issues, rooftop solar panels have taken off, now making up about a quarter of electricity use in the country. Similarly, drivers in Vietnam are increasingly opting for cheap electric vehicles from China, which now make up more than 40% of its car sales.
paras.zh: 而且，由于化石燃料价格高昂，许多发展中国家的消费者无需等待援助就掌握了清洁技术。在巴基斯坦，受到停电和电网供应问题的困扰，屋顶太阳能电池板已经开始普及，目前约占该国用电量的四分之一。同样，越南的司机越来越多地选择来自中国的廉价电动汽车，目前中国汽车占其汽车销量的 40% 以上。

paras.en: Meanwhile, the conference hosts themselves, from unpromising beginnings, have brought forward one of the biggest new ideas in the last decade for putting the world on track to lower emissions – changing fuel sources for cars and heating to electricity. The electricity should be from clean sources where possible – but its efficiency means that even if the energy source is fossil-based, it still uses less power.
paras.zh: 与此同时，会议主办方从一开始并不乐观，提出了过去十年来让世界走上降低排放轨道的最大新想法之一——将汽车和供暖的燃料来源改为电力。电力应尽可能来自清洁能源，但其效率意味着即使能源是化石能源，它仍然使用更少的电力。

paras.en: Jan Rosenow, professor of energy and climate policy at Oxford University, estimates that the superior efficiency of electricity over fossil fuels will mean that the world’s total final energy use can be halved by switching to electric for everything – meaning we need to generate a lot less, too.
paras.zh: 牛津大学能源与气候政策教授扬·罗塞诺估计，电力相对于化石燃料的卓越效率意味着，通过一切都改用电力，世界最终能源使用总量可以减少一半，这意味着我们需要减少发电量。

paras.en: If countries can agree a target at Cop31 of deriving 35% of final energy use from electricity by 2035, up from 23% today, that would be a major boost to decarbonisation efforts. Adair Turner, former chair of the UK’s climate change committee and now co-chair of the Energy Transitions Commission thinktank, said: “Electrification is the single most important thing you have to do [to reach net zero emissions].”
paras.zh: 如果各国能够在第 31 届缔约方大会上商定一个目标，即到 2035 年，最终能源使用量的 35% 来自电力，高于目前的 23%，这将极大推动脱碳工作。英国气候变化委员会前主席、现任能源转型委员会智囊团联合主席阿代尔·特纳表示：“电气化是[实现净零排放]必须做的最重要的事情。”

paras.en: Cops provide a place where countries can come together to share experiences, to seek advice, to find support and fellowship. “That’s very valuable,” said Ilana Seid, ambassador of Palau and chair of the Pacific Small Island Developing States. And in a world in which the bulk of current and future emissions, and fossil fuel production, comes from non-democracies or authoritarian states, Cops also provides one of the few forums where they can be held to account.
paras.zh: 警察提供了一个各国可以聚集在一起分享经验、寻求建议、寻求支持和友谊的场所。 “这非常有价值，”帕劳大使兼太平洋小岛屿发展中国家主席伊拉娜·赛义德说。在当前和未来的大部分排放以及化石燃料生产都来自非民主国家或独裁国家的世界中，警察组织还提供了为数不多的可以追究他们责任的论坛之一。

paras.en: That “societal pressure” is crucial, said Seid. “We small islands and vulnerable nations are on the frontline. For us, this is existential. We are all very committed to Paris.”
paras.zh: 塞德说，“社会压力”至关重要。 “我们这些小岛屿和脆弱国家处于前线。对我们来说，这是生死攸关的事情。我们都非常致力于巴黎。”

paras.en: After all, despite all the doubts, the power of a decision at Cop should not be underestimated. While “coalitions of the willing” are a “good thing” according to Nick Stern, the economist, the universality of the Paris agreement and Cops give them a unique authority.
paras.zh: 毕竟，尽管存在种种疑问，警察局决策的力量仍不容低估。虽然经济学家尼克·斯特恩认为“自愿联盟”是一件“好事”，但《巴黎协定》和《警察》的普遍性赋予了他们独特的权威。

paras.en: Sue Biniaz, a former US climate negotiator, said: “Any time you have a consensus decision, it sends a signal to investors, to people who finance things, and to countries. I think that’s true these days with the geopolitics of the world – if something can be agreed by the whole world, it’s impactful.”
paras.zh: 美国前气候谈判代表苏·比尼亚兹(Sue Biniaz)表示：“任何时候达成共识决定，都会向投资者、融资者和国家发出信号。我认为当今世界的地缘政治确实如此——如果某件事能够得到全世界的一致同意，那么它就会产生影响。”

paras.en: Cop31 may bring progress on electrification, on climate finance and on the transition that countries, rich and poor, need to make to a low-carbon world. But we already know that whatever the summit produces, it will not be enough.
paras.zh: 第三十一届缔约方会议可能会在电气化、气候融资以及各国（无论贫富）向低碳世界转型方面取得进展。但我们已经知道，无论峰会产生什么成果，都还不够。

paras.en: However flawed yet substantive they are, Cops last only a fortnight, while efforts to tackle the climate crisis will require such wholesale transformation of our economies and societies that they should top governments’ agendas all year.
paras.zh: 无论它们有多么缺陷和实质性，它们只能持续两周，而解决气候危机的努力将需要我们的经济和社会进行大规模转型，因此它们应该成为政府全年议程的首要议题。

paras.en: “Imagine you have lost your loved one without having their bodies to bring back home. Lost livelihood where you spent your whole life to accumulate those assets. We faced a horrific situation,” said Sujeeta Mathema, executive director of ActionAid Nepal, who was quickly on the scene to help people after the catastrophic glacier collapse there.
paras.zh: “想象一下，你失去了你所爱的人，却没有把他们的尸体带回家。你失去了你一生都在积累这些资产的生计。我们面临着可怕的情况，”尼泊尔行动援助组织执行董事苏吉塔·马蒂马说，他在灾难性冰川崩塌后迅速赶到现场帮助人们。

paras.en: “It feels like living with grief, fear and uncertainty about the future. The devastation is not just physical; it is deeply emotional and psychological.”
paras.zh: “感觉就像生活在悲伤、恐惧和对未来的不确定之中。这种破坏不仅是身体上的，也是深刻的情感和心理上的。”

paras.en: People are traumatised, she says, and deeply feel the injustice of how the climate crisis is created by the rich while hurting the most vulnerable. But Cop can still be a place of hope, Mathema adds.
paras.zh: 她说，人们受到了创伤，并深深感受到富人制造气候危机同时伤害最弱势群体的不公正。但马西马补充道，科普仍然是一个充满希望的地方。

paras.en: “Cop is an important space for us to raise our voice, clearly putting our agenda. Cop can help prevent such disasters if the commitments come off paper and are put into action.”
paras.zh: “Cop 是我们发出声音、明确提出议程的重要空间。如果承诺落实在纸上并付诸行动，Cop 就可以帮助预防此类灾难。”

articles.title: US midterm results may help unite Israeli coalition to unseat Netanyahu
articles.author: Emma Graham-Harrison in Jerusalem

paras.en: The Democrats’ sweep of Congress may make it easier for Israel’s splintered opposition to overcome deep internal divisions and form a coalition government, by increasing the urgency of unseating Benjamin Netanyahu, who has associated himself so closely with Donald Trump’s Republicans.
paras.zh: 民主党横扫国会可能会让以色列分裂的反对派更容易克服深刻的内部分歧并组建联合政府，因为这增加了推翻与唐纳德·特朗普的共和党关系密切的本杰明·内塔尼亚胡的紧迫性。

paras.en: But as Israel took stock of the results, there was also a sense that the elections marked a longer-term shift in US politics that will make the job of any new Israeli leader far more difficult.
paras.zh: 但当以色列评估选举结果时，人们也感觉到这次选举标志着美国政治的长期转变，这将使以色列新领导人的工作变得更加困难。

paras.en: The United States provides Israel with critical military and diplomatic support, so nurturing bipartisan ties was the cornerstone of foreign policy for decades. Netanyahu ripped up that commitment to throw his lot in with the Republicans in general and Trump in particular.
paras.zh: 美国为以色列提供重要的军事和外交支持，因此培育两党关系是几十年来外交政策的基石。内塔尼亚胡撕毁了这一承诺，将自己的命运投向共和党，特别是特朗普。

paras.en: The opposition had always attacked his decision as ill-judged. By the end of the week, they were warning that it was positively dangerous.
paras.zh: 反对派一直批评他的决定判断失误。到本周末，他们警告说这是非常危险的。

paras.en: “These people aren’t against Israel,” prominent opposition politician Yair Lapid said of incoming Democratic lawmakers, urging his country to rebuild bridges. “They’re mainly against Netanyahu – for them, anything connected to him is toxic.”
paras.zh: “这些人并不反对以色列，”著名反对派政治家亚伊尔·拉皮德在谈到即将上任的民主党议员时说道，并敦促他的国家重建桥梁。 “他们主要反对内塔尼亚胡——对他们来说，任何与他有关的东西都是有毒的。”

paras.en: “The easiest thing is to scream that ‘America is lost,’ because if it’s lost, you don’t have to work. That’s just not true. Not at all.”
paras.zh: “最简单的事情就是尖叫‘美国迷失了’，因为如果它迷失了，你就不必工作。这不是真的。根本不是。”

paras.en: Lapid laid out a plan to “rebuild trust” in the US, but it perhaps did more to demonstrate the scale of the problem than reassure Israelis.
paras.zh: 拉皮德制定了一项在美国“重建信任”的计划，但它可能更多地展示了问题的严重性，而不是安抚以色列人。

paras.en: His proposal of a transatlantic charm offensive by officials of a prospective new government drew a swift and sharp rebuke from the New York congressman-elect Brad Lander.
paras.zh: 他提出的由未来新政府官员发起跨大西洋魅力攻势的提议遭到了纽约当选国会议员布拉德·兰德的迅速而尖锐的谴责。

paras.en: Lander, a Democrat who is Jewish and describes himself as a liberal Zionist, was detained in the occupied West Bank last month while joining Palestinians trying to harvest olives.
paras.zh: 兰德是一名犹太人，民主党人，自称是自由犹太复国主义者，上个月在被占领的约旦河西岸与巴勒斯坦人一起试图收获橄榄时被拘留。

paras.en: “Minister Lapid: As someone who won a seat in Congress last night, and who cares about Israel: you’re not listening to what American voters – Jewish and non-Jewish – are saying,” Lander wrote in a direct response.
paras.zh: 兰德在直接回应中写道：“拉皮德部长：作为昨晚在国会赢得席位、关心以色列的人：你没有倾听美国选民——犹太人和非犹太人——的言论。”

paras.en: “We aren’t starving for a barnstorming tour. We’re hungry to see respect for international law and human rights.”
paras.zh: “我们并不渴望巡回演出。我们渴望看到对国际法和人权的尊重。”

paras.en: In his exchange with Lapid, Lander also highlighted the arrest of journalist Abed Abu Shehada, a Palestinian citizen of Israel, as an example of how Israel violates international law. He drew a direct link with the ICE “regime of detention without charges, based on secret evidence, designed to intimidate and chill speech” that he said was rejected by US voters.
paras.zh: 在与拉皮德的交流中，兰德还强调了以色列巴勒斯坦公民记者阿贝德·阿布·谢哈达的被捕，作为以色列违反国际法的一个例子。他与 ICE 的“基于秘密证据、旨在恐吓和镇压言论的未经指控的拘留制度”建立了直接联系，他说这种制度遭到了美国选民的拒绝。

paras.en: Abu Shehada was reportedly taken from his home by 15 masked security officials in a night-time raid, without an arrest warrant. Interrogators have only questioned him about a podcast interview with a public figure, lawyers acting for Abu Shehada said.
paras.zh: 据报道，阿布·谢哈达 (Abu Shehada) 在一次夜间突袭中被 15 名蒙面安全官员从家中带走，而且没有逮捕令。阿布·谢哈达的代理律师表示，审讯人员只是就对一位公众人物的播客采访对他进行了讯问。

paras.en: On Friday, Lander and two other incoming Jewish members of Congress, Daniel Bliss and Scott Wiener, wrote to Israel’s ambassador to the US calling for the immediate release of Abu Shehada.
paras.zh: 周五，兰德和另外两名即将上任的犹太国会议员丹尼尔·布利斯和斯科特·维纳写信给以色列驻美国大使，呼吁立即释放阿布·谢哈达。

paras.en: “Detaining a reporter for conducting an interview — the only issue that interrogators questioned him about — is a violation of international law,” Lander said when he published the letter. “It comes at a time when senior Israeli officials are trying to delegitimize the participation of Palestinian citizens in Israel’s recent elections.”
paras.zh: 兰德在发表这封信时表示：“拘留一名进行采访的记者——审讯人员询问他的唯一问题——违反了国际法。” “此时以色列高级官员正试图剥夺巴勒斯坦公民参与以色列最近选举的合法性。”

paras.en: Nor do Israel’s problems end with angry Democrats. The wounded Republican establishment lost no time looking a few thousand miles away to find reasons for the collapse of its voter base.
paras.zh: 以色列的问题也不会因愤怒的民主党人而结束。受伤的共和党建制派不失时机地向几千英里外寻找其选民基础崩溃的原因。

paras.en: Soon after the election results came in, the vice-president, JD Vance, put “our relationship with Israel” on a short list of reasons for voter fury, and on election day Trump made a last-ditch attempt to woo voters with a pledge to cut off $4bn (£3bn) in annual military aid to Israel.
paras.zh: 选举结果公布后不久，副总统 J·D·万斯 (JD Vance) 将“我们与以色列的关系”列入了选民愤怒的简短理由清单，而在选举日，特朗普做出了最后一搏，承诺削减对以色列每年 40 亿美元（30 亿英镑）的军事援助，以吸引选民。

paras.en: The announcement caused panic in Israel’s defence establishment. “When the commander of the Israel air force hears something like that, he might slit his wrists,” one official told Channel 12 news. “Where are we going to come up with 15 billion shekels every year, and what does that mean for Israel’s future defence budget?”
paras.zh: 这一消息引起了以色列国防机构的恐慌。 “当以色列空军指挥官听到这样的事情时，他可能会割腕，”一名官员告诉第 12 频道新闻。 “我们每年从哪里拿出 150 亿谢克尔，这对以色列未来的国防预算意味着什么？”

paras.en: Netanyahu only responded to Trump’s electioneering on Friday with an attempt to spin the cut as a joint decision reflecting Israel’s economic strength. It demonstrated a “move from aid to partnership”, his office said in a statement.
paras.zh: 内塔尼亚胡周五才对特朗普的竞选活动做出回应，试图将降息作为反映以色列经济实力的联合决定。他的办公室在一份声明中表示，这表明“从援助到伙伴关系的转变”。

paras.en: Netanyahu has long flaunted his relationship with Trump, his fluent English and experience in the US, presenting himself as the only man with the international standing to guarantee Israel’s security in a hostile world.
paras.zh: 内塔尼亚胡长期以来一直炫耀他与特朗普的关系、他流利的英语和在美国的经验，将自己描绘成唯一具有国际地位、能够在敌对世界中保障以色列安全的人。

paras.en: After Tuesday’s US election, he looks more like an agent of its destruction to many in Israel. “One thing is clear: we are losing America,” Ben Caspit wrote in Ma’ariv, a daily newspaper.
paras.zh: 在周二的美国大选之后，对于许多以色列人来说，他看起来更像是破坏美国大选的代理人。 “有一件事是明确的：我们正在失去美国，”本·卡斯皮特在《Ma’ariv》日报上写道。

paras.en: “This isn’t a process; it isn’t happening in stages; it is happening all at once. It is an avalanche. It is a reverberating collapse of the foundation of Israel’s national defence doctrine. This isn’t a decree of fate. It is a decree of Netanyahu.”
paras.zh: “这不是一个过程；它不是分阶段发生的；它是同时发生的。这是一场雪崩。这是以色列国防学说基础的彻底崩溃。这不是命运的法令。这是内塔尼亚胡的法令。”

paras.en: Some advocates for change inside Israel found cause for hope in the Democrats’ victory, if Israel’s opposition can turn their mandate for change into a new government. They won 67 seats in the 120-seat Knesset, but more than a quarter went to Palestinian citizens of Israel, and some of the Jewish Israeli opposition parties have ruled out sitting with them.
paras.zh: 如果以色列反对派能够将他们的变革使命转变为新政府，那么以色列内部的一些变革倡导者就对民主党的胜利抱有希望。他们在议会 120 个席位中赢得了 67 个席位，但超过四分之一的席位给了以色列的巴勒斯坦公民，一些以色列犹太反对党已经排除了与他们坐在一起的可能性。

paras.en: US administrations have for too long equated support for Israel with blind support for its government, said Nadav Tamir, a former senior Israeli diplomat in the US who is now executive director of J Street Israel.
paras.zh: 以色列前驻美高级外交官、现任 J Street Israel 执行董事纳达夫·塔米尔 (Nadav Tamir) 表示，美国政府长期以来一直将对以色列的支持等同于对其政府的盲目支持。

paras.en: That consensus is cracking, but the majority of lawmakers from both parties still see Israel as a key US ally in the Middle East, he wrote in the Times of Israel.
paras.zh: 他在《以色列时报》上写道，这种共识正在破裂，但两党的大多数立法者仍​​然将以色列视为美国在中东的重要盟友。

paras.en: External pressure from those who support its security but see current policy as self-destructive might push the country towards necessary change, including a resolution of the Israel-Palestine conflict.
paras.zh: 来自那些支持其安全但认为当前政策具有自我毁灭性的人的外部压力可能会推动该国进行必要的变革，包括解决以色列-巴勒斯坦冲突。

paras.en: “Perhaps this will be the paradox of the new [US] Congress,” he wrote. “It will be less willing to define support for Israel as automatic alignment with every policy of its government, but precisely for that reason, it may offer Israel more meaningful support in breaking out of the cycle of wars and building a future of security and prosperity.”
paras.zh: “也许这将成为新[美国]国会的悖论，”他写道。 “它不太愿意将对以色列的支持定义为自动与其政府的每项政策保持一致，但正是因为这个原因，它可能会为以色列提供更有意义的支持，帮助其摆脱战争循环并建设安全与繁荣的未来。”

articles.title: The young Somali woman changing how the world sees Mogadishu

paras.en: As the sun rises over the Indian Ocean, waves lap onto the golden sands while palm fronds rustle in the cool sea breeze. Welcome to... Mogadishu.
paras.zh: 当太阳从印度洋升起时，海浪拍打着金色的沙滩，棕榈叶在凉爽的海风中沙沙作响。欢迎来到...摩加迪沙。

paras.en: This is the image that one young Somali woman wants the world to have of her home city - in contrast to the one of suicide attacks and young men wielding AK-47s that many people currently associate with Somalia's capital.
paras.zh: 这是一位年轻的索马里妇女希望世界对她的家乡有这样的印象——与目前许多人将索马里首都联系在一起的自杀式袭击和挥舞 AK-47 的年轻男子的形象形成鲜明对比。

paras.en: Sucdi Abdul Fattah Abdul Khader is among a growing number of local guides taking visitors beyond the headlines to explore Mogadishu's beauty spots, historic sites and culture.
paras.zh: 苏克迪·阿卜杜勒·法塔赫·阿卜杜勒·卡德尔 (Sucdi Abdul Fattah Abdul Khader) 是越来越多的当地导游之一，他们带领游客超越头条新闻，探索摩加迪沙的美丽景点、历史遗迹和文化。

paras.en: Her favourite spot is Jazeera beach, where visitors can enjoy the sea before heading to nearby sand dunes.
paras.zh: 她最喜欢的地方是半岛海滩，游客可以在那里欣赏大海，然后前往附近的沙丘。

paras.en: "It's one of the tourist attractions where we bring our guests. It's a nice place," says the 23-year-old.
paras.zh: “这是我们带客人来的旅游景点之一。这是一个不错的地方，”这位 23 岁的年轻人说道。

paras.en: The dunes, she adds, remind some visitors of the Sahara.
paras.zh: 她补充道，这些沙丘让一些游客想起了撒哈拉沙漠。

paras.en: But her tours are about more than scenic views. She also takes visitors to the fish market, where they discover the variety of marine life available along Somalia's extensive coastline and to parts of the city that reflect its history as a busy Indian Ocean trading centre, with the influences of both its Ottoman and Italian former rulers.
paras.zh: 但她的旅行不仅仅是为了欣赏风景。她还带游客参观鱼市，在那里他们可以发现索马里广阔海岸线上的各种海洋生物，并参观该城市的部分地区，这些地区反映了该市作为繁忙的印度洋贸易中心的历史，并受到奥斯曼和意大利前统治者的影响。

paras.en: Visitors can also sample Somali food, including camel meat, samosas and traditional tea.
paras.zh: 游客还可以品尝索马里美食，包括骆驼肉、萨摩萨三角饺和传统茶。

paras.en: Sucdi says many arrive in the city with expectations shaped by years of hearing about the insecurity.
paras.zh: 苏迪说，许多人来到这座城市时都怀着因多年来听说不安全局势而产生的期望。

paras.en: "Mostly, they are surprised by how beautiful the country is and how welcoming people are," she says.
paras.zh: “大多数情况下，他们对这个国家的美丽和人们的热情感到惊讶，”她说。

paras.en: At the fish market, she says, visitors are particularly impressed by the variety of fish species.
paras.zh: 她说，在鱼市场，游客对鱼类种类的多样性印象特别深刻。

paras.en: Guiding tours runs in Sucdi's family. Her father worked in the profession for over three decades, taking journalists, photographers and visitors from different countries around Somalia.
paras.zh: Sucdi 家族经营导游服务。她的父亲在这个行业工作了三十多年，接待了来自索马里各地不同国家的记者、摄影师和游客。

paras.en: He introduced her to the business nearly three years ago.
paras.zh: 大约三年前，他向她介绍了这个行业。

paras.en: "I started this job as a hobby, but it has become something that I like and am passionate about," she says.
paras.zh: “我开始这份工作是出于一种爱好，但它已经成为我喜欢并充满热情的事情，”她说。

paras.en: She now works alongside her father and a team of guides, building on his experience while using social media to reach a wider audience.
paras.zh: 她现在与父亲和导游团队一起工作，借鉴父亲的经验，同时利用社交媒体接触更广泛的受众。

paras.en: She shares videos of her tours on TikTok, offering people outside Somalia a glimpse of places they may never have imagined visiting.
paras.zh: 她在 TikTok 上分享她的旅行视频，让索马里以外的人们一睹他们可能从未想象过的地方。

paras.en: She is also considering producing content in English to reach audiences who do not speak Somali.
paras.zh: 她还正在考虑制作英语内容，以吸引不会说索马里语的观众。

paras.en: Tourism remains a relatively new field in Somalia, she says, with only a handful working as guides in Mogadishu.
paras.zh: 她说，旅游业在索马里仍然是一个相对较新的领域，只有少数人在摩加迪沙担任导游。

paras.en: The business is seasonal, but Sucdi says this year has been particularly encouraging, although numbers are still fairly low. Having five tourists a week is considered a success but she is confident that numbers will grow.
paras.zh: 该业务是季节性的，但苏迪表示，今年的情况尤其令人鼓舞，尽管数量仍然相当低。每周接待五名游客被认为是成功的，但她相信数量将会增加。

paras.en: However, she says many visitors are still concerned about security.
paras.zh: 然而，她表示许多游客仍然担心安全问题。

paras.en: Since the collapse of Somalia's central government in 1991, Mogadishu has endured decades of civil war, destruction and displacement. Much of the city centre was reduced to rubble, and basic services and infrastructure largely broke down.
paras.zh: 自1991年索马里中央政府垮台以来，摩加迪沙经历了数十年的内战、破坏和流离失所。市中心大部分地区已化为废墟，基本服务和基础设施基本瘫痪。

paras.en: But following the withdrawal of the Islamist militant group al-Shabab from most of the city in 2011, and the establishment of the federal government in 2012, Mogadishu has undergone a gradual transformation.
paras.zh: 但随着2011年伊斯兰激进组织青年党从该市大部分地区撤出以及2012年联邦政府成立后，摩加迪沙逐渐发生了转变。

paras.en: Returning members of the Somali diaspora, local entrepreneurs and investors helped fuel a construction boom, with new hotels, restaurants, businesses and residential developments reshaping the capital.
paras.zh: 归国的索马里侨民、当地企业家和投资者推动了建筑热潮，新的酒店、餐馆、企业和住宅开发项目重塑了首都。

paras.en: Today, Mogadishu is a growing commercial hub, although insecurity and the legacy of conflict remain part of everyday life.
paras.zh: 如今，摩加迪沙已成为一个不断发展的商业中心，尽管不安全和冲突遗留问题仍然是日常生活的一部分。

paras.en: About 10,000 tourists visited Somalia in 2024, a 50% increase on the previous year, according to the country's tourism department.
paras.zh: 据该国旅游部门称，2024年将有约1万名游客前往索马里，比上一年增加50%。

paras.en: Many visitors ask about their safety before travelling and often encounter security checkpoints around the city.
paras.zh: 许多游客在旅行前都会询问自己的安全，并且经常会遇到城市周围的安全检查站。

paras.en: But she says their experience on the ground is generally positive.
paras.zh: 但她表示，他们的实地经验总体来说是积极的。

paras.en: "What they heard from the news and everywhere else is not the same as what they see in the country," she says.
paras.zh: “他们从新闻和其他地方听到的与他们在国内看到的不一样，”她说。

paras.en: Although some question whether Mogadishu is safe enough for a young woman to be working as a tour guide, Sucdi is determined to continue.
paras.zh: 尽管有人质疑摩加迪沙是否足够安全，适合一名年轻女性担任导游，但苏克迪决心继续下去。

paras.en: She wants visitors to experience a Somalia that is rarely seen.
paras.zh: 她希望游客体验一个罕见的索马里。

paras.en: "I would want them to see the beautiful, welcoming side of Mogadishu, and not the side that they heard from the media, which is explosions and bombs," she says.
paras.zh: “我希望他们看到摩加迪沙美丽、热情的一面，而不是他们从媒体上听到的爆炸和炸弹的一面，”她说。

paras.en: Somalia has Africa's longest mainland coastline, stretching more than 3,000km (1,860 miles) along the Indian Ocean and Gulf of Aden.
paras.zh: 索马里拥有非洲最长的大陆海岸线，沿着印度洋和亚丁湾绵延超过 3,000 公里（1,860 英里）。

paras.en: Its beaches and sand dunes sit alongside historic coastal cities such as Mogadishu, whose culture reflects centuries of Indian Ocean trade.
paras.zh: 它的海滩和沙丘毗邻摩加迪沙等历史悠久的沿海城市，其文化反映了几个世纪的印度洋贸易。

paras.en: For some tourists, that contrast between the country's reputation and what they experience can be striking.
paras.zh: 对于一些游客来说，这个国家的声誉与他们的经历之间的反差可能是惊人的。

paras.en: American travel content creator Chris Reese, who goes by the name Authentic Travelling, has visited Mogadishu twice.
paras.zh: 美国旅游内容创作者克里斯·里斯（Chris Reese），绰号“Authentic Travelling”，曾两次访问摩加迪沙。

paras.en: His first trip, almost a year ago, was a solo visit. He enjoyed it so much that he decided to return with a group of friends, who had seen videos of his visit on social media.
paras.zh: 大约一年前，他的第一次旅行是单独访问。他非常喜欢这次旅行，因此决定与一群朋友一起回来，他们在社交媒体上看过他的访问视频。

paras.en: "I had such a positive experience - I really enjoyed seeing the country for the first time - that I opted to bring back a group of my friends," he says.
paras.zh: “我有一次非常积极的经历——我真的很喜欢第一次看到这个国家——所以我选择带一群朋友回来，”他说。

paras.en: What stands out for Chris is the city's coastal setting, its food and atmosphere.
paras.zh: 对克里斯来说，最引人注目的是这座城市的沿海环境、美食和氛围。

paras.en: "It is such a beautiful tropical place. I love the vibe, the weather and the food," he says.
paras.zh: “这是一个美丽的热带地方。我喜欢这里的氛围、天气和食物，”他说。

paras.en: During the group's visit, they enjoy lunch overlooking the Indian Ocean before heading out to explore the beaches and sand dunes.
paras.zh: 在访问期间，他们一边享用午餐一边俯瞰印度洋，然后出发去探索海滩和沙丘。

paras.en: "The desert is beautiful and picturesque. It is also amazing that it's barely a 30-minute drive from Mogadishu," he says.
paras.zh: “沙漠美丽如画。令人惊奇的是，这里距离摩加迪沙仅 30 分钟车程，”他说。

paras.en: Before his first trip, Chris says, much of what he knew about Somalia came from international news coverage.
paras.zh: 克里斯说，在第一次旅行之前，他对索马里的了解大部分来自国际新闻报道。

paras.en: "If you only read the news reports about Somalia, you would be scared to visit. And honestly, that's what I saw in the media before I came, mostly negative headlines."
paras.zh: “如果你只看有关索马里的新闻报道，你会害怕去访问。说实话，这就是我来之前在媒体上看到的，大部分是负面的头条新闻。”

paras.en: But visiting the country challenged those perceptions.
paras.zh: 但访问该国挑战了这些看法。

paras.en: "Coming here, on my very first trip, showed me that there is so much more to this country than what is shown in the headlines," he says.
paras.zh: “第一次来到这里，我就发现这个国家的内涵远比头条新闻中所展示的要多得多，”他说。

paras.en: Mihaela Patap, from Romania, loves Somalia's natural beauty.
paras.zh: 来自罗马尼亚的 Mihaela Patap 热爱索马里的自然美景。

paras.en: Although she has spent only a few hours in Mogadishu, she has already visited the sand dunes and taken in the Indian Ocean coastline.
paras.zh: 尽管她在摩加迪沙只待了几个小时，但她已经参观了沙丘并拍摄了印度洋海岸线。

paras.en: "The desert was so beautiful to see. I have also enjoyed the beach, and the ocean. It is inspiring," she says.
paras.zh: “沙漠非常美丽。我也很喜欢海滩和海洋。这令人鼓舞，”她说。

paras.en: Having travelled to Somalia from neighbouring Ethiopia, she says she has been struck by the people's friendliness.
paras.zh: 她从邻国埃塞俄比亚来到索马里，她说当地人的友善给她留下了深刻的印象。

paras.en: "I don't see anything dangerous. I feel safe and the people are warm," she says.
paras.zh: “我没有看到任何危险。我感到安全，人们很温暖，”她说。

paras.en: An experienced traveller, Mihaela says she prefers to visit new countries without having preconceived ideas.
paras.zh: 米哈埃拉是一位经验丰富的旅行者，她说她更喜欢在没有先入为主的想法的情况下游览新的国家。

paras.en: "I travel the world to see new places, to see countries, to see the differences. I don't take a picture in my mind to compare the reality with. I'm just expecting the new to come to me," she says.
paras.zh: “我环游世界去看看新的地方，看看各个国家，看看差异。我不会在脑海中拍一张照片来与现实进行比较。我只是期待新的事物降临到我身上，”她说。

paras.en: She hopes to share her experience and encourage others to visit Somalia.
paras.zh: 她希望分享自己的经历并鼓励其他人访问索马里。

paras.en: "I'm going to post my pictures and say good things about what I'm experiencing. I'm going to promote it," she says.
paras.zh: “我会发布我的照片，并对我所经历的事情说一些好话。我会宣传它，”她说。

paras.en: She is continuing a family profession while building a business in an industry with few women and using digital platforms to reach audiences far beyond Mogadishu.
paras.zh: 她继续从事家庭职业，同时在一个女性很少的行业中开展业务，并利用数字平台吸引远远超出摩加迪沙的受众。

paras.en: "Somalia still has a long way to go before tourism becomes a major industry," she says.
paras.zh: “在旅游业成为主要产业之前，索马里还有很长的路要走，”她说。

paras.en: "Through my tours, I am giving visitors an opportunity to experience its landscapes, our culture and people beyond the familiar negative headlines."
paras.zh: “通过我的旅行，我让游客有机会体验这里的风景、我们的文化和人民，超越熟悉的负面头条新闻。”

paras.en: For her, every visitor is another opportunity to tell a fuller story of Mogadishu.
paras.zh: 对她来说，每一位游客都是讲述摩加迪沙更完整故事的另一个机会。

articles.title: This man refused life-saving treatment because of his religion - days later the rules changed

paras.en: In August this year, 26-year-old Isaac Valdez had an epileptic seizure while browsing in his local library, causing him to convulse and strike his head against the ground.
paras.zh: 今年8月，26岁的艾萨克·瓦尔迪兹(Isaac Valdez)在当地图书馆浏览时癫痫发作，导致他全身抽搐，头撞在地上。

paras.en: He lost consciousness. Later, in hospital, it transpired Isaac had hit his head with such force it had led to a brain haemorrhage.
paras.zh: 他失去了知觉。后来，在医院里，艾萨克用力撞击头部，导致脑出血。

paras.en: Treatment was seriously complicated by the fact that, as a Jehovah's Witness, Isaac carried a "No Blood" card, an indication that he would not accept treatment involving any form of blood transfusion because of his religious beliefs.
paras.zh: 作为一名耶和华见证人教徒，艾萨克携带着一张“禁止输血”卡，这表明他由于宗教信仰而不会接受任何形式的输血治疗，这使得治疗变得非常复杂。

paras.en: As a result, a procedure to drain fluid from Isaac's brain did not take place.
paras.zh: 结果，没有进行从艾萨克大脑中排出液体的手术。

paras.en: But his family, from Waxahachie, Texas, were encouraged by the fact that he regained consciousness and even started to talk again. He was able to confirm that he stood by his "no blood" beliefs.
paras.zh: 但他来自德克萨斯州沃克西哈奇的家人对他恢复知觉、甚至再次开始说话感到鼓舞。他能够确认自己坚持“没有血统”的信念。

paras.en: The family's relief at his apparent improvement was short-lived. Isaac slipped into a coma and his condition worsened rapidly.
paras.zh: 家人因他的明显好转而松了一口气，但这种安慰并没有持续太久。艾萨克陷入昏迷，病情迅速恶化。

paras.en: A neurosurgeon told Isaac's family the only way to save his life was an emergency operation, but that it was one that required blood transfusion.
paras.zh: 一名神经外科医生告诉艾萨克的家人，挽救他生命的唯一方法是紧急手术，但需要输血。

paras.en: His family took the decision to abide by Issac's wishes as a lifelong Witness not to accept such a procedure.
paras.zh: 他的家人决定遵守伊萨克作为终身见证人的愿望，不接受这样的程序。

paras.en: Isaac - who his twin brother Jacob Valdez describes as an intelligent man who loved volunteering and helping the elderly - died on 26 August 2026 when doctors turned off his life support.
paras.zh: 艾萨克（Isaac）——他的双胞胎兄弟雅各布·瓦尔迪兹（Jacob Valdez）形容他是一位聪明人，热爱志愿服务和帮助老年人——于 2026 年 8 月 26 日去世，当时医生关闭了他的生命支持系统。

paras.en: Just 23 days later, the Jehovah's Witnesses' Governing Body announced a seismic change in teaching that would, in effect, have given Isaac the religious green light to have the life-saving treatment he had refused.
paras.zh: 仅仅 23 天后，耶和华见证人的中央长老团宣布在教义上发生翻天覆地的变化，这实际上为以撒开了宗教绿灯，允许他接受他拒绝的救命治疗。

paras.en: The change suddenly means the vast majority of medical procedures using donated blood are no longer prohibited to followers. Now, decisions on whether to accept such treatments are to be left to individuals.
paras.zh: 这一变化突然意味着绝大多数使用捐献血液的医疗程序不再禁止追随者。现在，是否接受此类治疗的决定由个人决定。

paras.en: Jacob, already dealing with the death of his twin, was angered at the Jehovah's Witnesses' leadership for not coming to their conclusion sooner. He told BBC News he believes Isaac could well still be alive if they had.
paras.zh: 雅各布已经在处理他双胞胎的死亡问题，他对耶和华见证人的领导层没有尽快得出结论感到愤怒。他告诉英国广播公司新闻，他相信如果他们有的话，艾萨克很可能还活着。

paras.en: The original rule on blood transfusions dates back to 1945, towards the very end of a war during which the use of blood transfusions had been increasingly widespread. The leaders of Jehovah's Witnesses announced that their believers were not permitted to accept transfusions.
paras.zh: 关于输血的最初规定可以追溯到 1945 年，战争即将结束时，输血的使用越来越普遍。耶和华见证人的领袖宣布，他们的信徒不得接受输血。

paras.en: This was based on their interpretation of Bible verses from both the Old and New Testaments prohibiting the consumption of blood, including one from the Book of Acts that instructs believers to abstain from blood, from food offered to idols, and from things that had been strangled.
paras.zh: 这是基于他们对《旧约》和《新约》中禁止吃血的圣经经文的解释，其中包括《使徒行传》中的一节，指示信徒禁戒血、祭偶像的食物和勒死的东西。

paras.en: So, why has the Jehovah's Witnesses' Governing Body, based in New York state, now decided to change the rules, 81 years after introducing them?
paras.zh: 那么，为什么总部位于纽约州的耶和华见证人中央长老团在推出这些规则 81 年后，现在又决定改变这些规则呢？

paras.en: It comes after years of pressure from both within and outside the faith, but that is not how leaders of the faith describe the decision.
paras.zh: 这是在多年来来自信仰内部和外部的压力之后做出的，但这并不是信仰领袖描述这一决定的方式。

paras.en: "The change is basically the application of Bible principles to modern medicine and its methods," says the Jehovah's Witnesses international spokesperson, Paul Gillies, who described it as both a fresh look at scripture and at medical advances.
paras.zh: 耶和华见证人国际发言人保罗·吉利斯说：“这一变化基本上是将圣经原则应用于现代医学及其方法。”他将其描述为对圣经和医学进步的新看法。

paras.en: We meet Gillies at the Jehovah's Witnesses UK headquarters set in 85 acres of Essex countryside. It is a vast modern complex where hundreds of volunteer followers of the faith live and work without pay.
paras.zh: 我们在位于埃塞克斯乡村占地 85 英亩的耶和华见证人英国总部见到了吉利斯。这是一个巨大的现代化建筑群，数百名信仰志愿者在这里无薪生活和工作。

paras.en: He insists the basic teaching has not changed and that the transfusion of whole blood is still prohibited. However, for decades, most transfusions have not used whole blood, instead using the specific components of blood that are needed by the patient.
paras.zh: 他坚称基本教学没有改变，输全血仍然被禁止。然而，几十年来，大多数输血都没有使用全血，而是使用患者所需的特定血液成分。

paras.en: The change is being justified by permitting the use of blood components, like plasma and red blood cells and platelets, in the huge numbers of medical procedures that were previously banned.
paras.zh: 这一变化是合理的，因为允许在以前被禁止的大量医疗程序中使用血浆、红细胞和血小板等血液成分。

paras.en: Gillies says the Bible references "abstaining from blood" but not "various components that could be extracted from blood".
paras.zh: 吉利斯说，圣经提到“禁戒血液”，但没有提到“可以从血液中提取的各种成分”。

paras.en: He says the Governing Body felt it their duty to avoid scriptural "overreach" and only apply what was specifically described in the Bible.
paras.zh: 他说，中央长老团认为自己有责任避免“超越圣经”，只应用圣经中具体描述的内容。

paras.en: But that explanation has stunned many and led them to ask if it was not a huge overreach 81 years ago to ban blood transfusions in the first place, when transfusions are not specifically mentioned in the bible.
paras.zh: 但这一解释让许多人感到震惊，并让他们质疑，81 年前圣经中没有具体提到输血，而一开始就禁止输血，这是否是一种过分的行为。

paras.en: Others are then also asking why it has taken so long to come to this landmark decision, given that transfusions that do not use whole blood have been the norm for decades.
paras.zh: 其他人也在问，鉴于几十年来不使用全血的输血已成为常态，为什么花了这么长时间才做出这一具有里程碑意义的决定。

paras.en: These are questions Jacob asked as soon as the ban was lifted, just days after a memorial service for Isaac.
paras.zh: 这些是雅各布在禁令解除后提出的问题，就在艾萨克追悼会几天后。

paras.en: Jacob, who had already left the Jehovah's Witness faith he was brought up in, texted prominent figures from Isaac's congregation in Texas after Isaac's death. The messages are full of angst, and painful to read.
paras.zh: 雅各布已经离开了他长大的耶和华见证人信仰，在以撒死后，他给德克萨斯州以撒会众的知名人士发了短信。这些信息充满了焦虑，读起来很痛苦。

paras.en: He asked them to consider "the part you played in encouraging so many people to sacrifice their life for something that was never God's will".
paras.zh: 他要求他们考虑一下“你在鼓励这么多人为了一些从来不符合上帝意愿的事情而牺牲自己的生命方面所扮演的角色”。

paras.en: Most did not reply, but one "elder" responded saying he could not understand why Jacob was so angry and fixated on the policy shift.
paras.zh: 大多数人没有回复，但一位“长老”回应说，他不明白为什么雅各布如此愤怒并专注于政策转变。

paras.en: This all further infuriated Jacob, who particularly wants the faith's decision-makers to be accountable for all the lives lost.
paras.zh: 这一切进一步激怒了雅各布，他特别希望该信仰的决策者对所有逝去的生命负责。

paras.en: "I want to ask them if they could apologise directly, I would like not to have a deflected answer, just straightforward apology," he says.
paras.zh: “我想问他们是否可以直接道歉，我不希望得到偏颇的答案，只是直接道歉，”他说。

paras.en: It is extremely difficult to say how many Jehovah's Witnesses, among the estimated nine million followers of the faith worldwide, died each year having refused treatment involving blood transfusions. But research in one medical journal in 2016, The Obstetrical & Gynecological Survey, put the figure at around 1,100.
paras.zh: 全世界估计有九百万耶和华见证人信徒，很难说每年有多少人因拒绝输血治疗而死亡。但 2016 年一份医学杂志《妇产科调查》的研究显示，这一数字约为 1,100。

paras.en: "We're sympathetic to their feelings, and if individuals have lost family members and are concerned about some of these questions, they deserve to be heard compassionately," says Gillies.
paras.zh: 吉利斯说：“我们同情他们的感受，如果有人失去了家人并担心其中一些问题，他们应该得到富有同情心的倾听。”

paras.en: But there was little clarity about why the change did not come earlier.
paras.zh: 但对于为什么没有更早进行这一改变还不清楚。

paras.en: "Why has it taken this time? Well, I guess because it takes time, it doesn't necessarily mean that there is some magic change that's taken place," says Gillies.
paras.zh: “为什么要花这个时间？嗯，我想因为这需要时间，这并不一定意味着发生了一些神奇的变化，”吉利斯说。

paras.en: And when asked, Gillies deflects calls for the leadership to apologise, saying that many lives had, in fact, been saved because faithful Jehovah's Witnesses had not been exposed to blood contamination scandals.
paras.zh: 当被问到时，吉利斯回避了要求领导层道歉的呼声，并表示，事实上，由于忠实的耶和华见证人没有受到血液污染丑闻的影响，许多人的生命得到了拯救。

paras.en: He also insists that even after the new edict, some Jehovah's Witnesses could still decide they did not want to accept a transfusion, and that may have been the case even if the edict had come years ago.
paras.zh: 他还坚称，即使在新法令颁布之后，一些耶和华见证人仍然可能决定不想接受输血，即使该法令是在几年前颁布的，情况也可能是这样。

paras.en: Indeed, the BBC spoke with Alex Ball, 58, a Jehovah's Witness from West Sussex, who says in 2012 a doctor told him he would not survive the chemotherapy he needed to treat his blood cancer unless he also had a transfusion.
paras.zh: 事实上，BBC 采访了来自西萨塞克斯的 58 岁耶和华见证人亚历克斯·鲍尔 (Alex Ball)，他说，2012 年，一位医生告诉他，如果不接受输血，他就无法在治疗血癌所需的化疗中存活下来。

paras.en: "I wanted to adhere as closely to the scriptures as possible when I was sick, and I think I did that well."
paras.zh: “当我生病时，我想尽可能严格遵守经文，我认为我做得很好。”

paras.en: With help from what is called "a Jehovah's Witness Hospital Liaison Committee", Alex found an American consultant who could perform a treatment to boost Alex's blood cells without the need for any products from someone else. His UK consultant agreed to treat him using the new method and it worked.
paras.zh: 在所谓的“耶和华见证人医院联络委员会”的帮助下，亚历克斯找到了一位美国顾问，他可以进行治疗来增强亚历克斯的血细胞，而不需要其他人的任何产品。他的英国顾问同意使用新方法治疗他，并且效果很好。

paras.en: More than a decade later, Alex says he would make the same decision again, despite the change in blood policy that would have permitted the transfusions he had been told he needed.
paras.zh: 十多年后，亚历克斯说他会再次做出同样的决定，尽管血液政策发生了变化，允许他被告知需要输血。

paras.en: It is not just receiving blood which has been an issue.
paras.zh: 问题不只是接受血液。

paras.en: Elisha Cummings, 50, a Jehovah's Witness from Trinidad and Tobago, was unable to donate blood to her aunt, who died, because of the rules.
paras.zh: 50 岁的伊莱莎·卡明斯 (Elisha Cummings) 是来自特立尼达和多巴哥的耶和华见证人，由于规定，她无法向去世的姨妈献血。

paras.en: They also cost her her marriage too, with her husband of 10 years leaving the faith and divorcing her after it came to light that he had had a blood transfusion as a child, something that was looked down upon in her Witness community.
paras.zh: 他们也让她失去了婚姻，她的丈夫在发现他小时候接受过输血后离开了信仰，并与她离婚，而这在她的见证人社区是被人看不起的。

paras.en: "Since the blood policy change, I have not been myself," she says. "It left me in a sort of depressed mode."
paras.zh: “自从血液政策改变后，我就不再是我自己了，”她说。 “这让我陷入了一种沮丧的状态。”

paras.en: "How many houses did I go to trying to convince people about the blood doctrine? And you're coming now and it's something totally different," Elisha says.
paras.zh: “我去了多少家试图让人们相信血统教义？而你现在来了，情况就完全不同了，”以利沙说。

paras.en: Elisha says her beliefs as a whole have been shaken, yet she feels reluctant to leave the faith, partly because it is what provides her with her community and she fears isolation.
paras.zh: 以利沙说，她的整体信仰已经动摇，但她不愿意放弃信仰，部分原因是信仰为她提供了社区，而她害怕孤立。

paras.en: In the past, those who disagreed with "blood doctrine" were ostracised or felt like they needed to leave the faith. Will they now be able to come back?
paras.zh: 过去，那些不同意“血统教义”的人受到排斥，或者觉得他们需要离开这个信仰。他们现在能回来吗？

paras.en: "Any individual that wants to come back to the faith is warmly welcomed," says Gillies, speaking of those who had left the faith because they had accepted a transfusion for themselves or a relative.
paras.zh: “任何想要回归信仰的人都会受到热烈欢迎，”吉利斯谈到那些因为为自己或亲戚接受输血而离开信仰的人时说。

paras.en: "If they would like to become one of Jehovah's Witnesses again and would like to speak to the elders, then they're very welcome to do so."
paras.zh: “如果他们想再次成为耶和华见证人之一，并愿意与长老交谈，那么我们非常欢迎他们这样做。”

articles.title: Paraguay's President Santiago Peña impeached and arrested

paras.en: Paraguay's President Santiago PeÃ±a has been impeached and placed under house arrest after the collapse of a digital bank with links to his private business interests.
paras.zh: 巴拉圭总统圣地亚哥·佩尼亚因一家与其私人商业利益有联系的数字银行倒闭而遭到弹劾并被软禁。

paras.en: PeÃ±a was arrested on Friday minutes after lawmakers, including from his own party, unanimously voted to remove him from office due to a widening crisis triggered by the collapse of Ueno Bank earlier this week.
paras.zh: 由于本周早些时候上野银行倒闭引发的危机不断扩大，佩尼亚于周五被捕，几分钟前，包括他所在政党在内的立法者一致投票罢免他的职务。

paras.en: He had offered to step down on Thursday. Rather than accept his resignation, senators impeached PeÃ±a and charged him with misconduct, meaning he has been stripped of the immunity usually granted to ex-presidents.
paras.zh: 他已于周四提出辞职。参议员们没有接受他的辞职，而是弹劾了佩尼亚并指控他行为不当，这意味着他被剥夺了通常授予前总统的豁免权。

paras.en: PeÃ±a, who until last year held shares in the company that owned the bank, has denied any wrongdoing.
paras.zh: 佩尼亚直到去年还持有该银行所属公司的股份，他否认有任何不当行为。

paras.en: The demise of the digital bank has left more than half of Paraguay's population without access to their savings after it was seized by Paraguay's central bank.
paras.zh: 数字银行的消亡导致巴拉圭中央银行没收数字银行后，超过一半的巴拉圭人口无法使用其储蓄。

paras.en: An estimated three million depositors remain unable to access their savings and pensions prompting widespread protests particularly in the capital, AsunciÃ³n.
paras.zh: 据估计，有 300 万储户仍然无法提取储蓄和养老金，引发了广泛的抗议活动，尤其是在首都亚松森。

paras.en: The impeachment charges that led to PeÃ±a's removal alleged he had conflicts of interest, manipulated regulatory oversight, diverted pension funds, and participated in an institutional cover-up involving the central bank.
paras.zh: 导致佩尼亚被免职的弹劾指控称他存在利益冲突、操纵监管、挪用养老基金以及参与涉及央行的机构掩盖行为。

paras.en: PeÃ±a is due to be questioned on Saturday over allegations of breach of trust, influence peddling, and misappropriation of funds, prosecutor Silvia Margarita Gonzalez Vester said.
paras.zh: 检察官西尔维娅·玛格丽塔·冈萨雷斯·维斯特表示，佩尼亚将于周六因违反信任、兜售影响力和挪用资金等指控接受讯问。

paras.en: PeÃ±a's impeachment passed with 44 out of 45 senators voting in favour of it. One lawmaker was absent.
paras.zh: 佩尼亚的弹劾案以 45 名参议员中的 44 人投了赞成票获得通过。一名议员缺席。

paras.en: Afterwards, senate president Basilio NÃºÃ±ez said PeÃ±a was found guilty of "dereliction of duty".
paras.zh: 随后，参议院议长巴西利奥·努涅斯表示，佩尼亚被判犯有“玩忽职守”罪。

paras.en: Paraguay's Vice-President Pedro Alliana was then sworn in as interim President.
paras.zh: 巴拉圭副总统佩德罗·阿利亚纳随后宣誓就任临时总统。

paras.en: "Compatriots who are now going through a difficult time as a result of the financial collapse will be fully compensated," said Alliana, who will serve as President until 2028.
paras.zh: 阿利亚纳将担任总统直至 2028 年，他表示：“由于金融崩溃而正在经历困难时期的同胞将得到充分补偿。”

paras.en: Senator Rafael Filizzola said: "We are facing the biggest corruption scandal in our democratic history â a tremendous blow to the state, to private citizens, and to the country's credibility and image."
paras.zh: 参议员拉斐尔·菲利佐拉表示：“我们正面临民主历史上最大的腐败丑闻——对国家、公民个人以及国家的信誉和形象造成巨大打击。”

paras.en: Analysts say PeÃ±a is likely to now be prosecuted over the bank's collapse.
paras.zh: 分析人士表示，佩尼亚现在可能会因银行倒闭而受到起诉。

paras.en: His defence lawyer Ricardo Preda described the allegations as a "reckless accusation" that was "irresponsible and opportunistic".
paras.zh: 他的辩护律师里卡多·普雷达称这些指控是“鲁莽的指控”，是“不负责任和机会主义的”。

paras.en: In an address to the nation on Thursday, PeÃ±a said that he was sorry and that "it was never my intention to betray the trust you placed in me".
paras.zh: 佩尼亚在周四向全国发表的讲话中表示，他很抱歉，并且“我从来没有打算背叛你们对我的信任”。

articles.title: How Paper-Based Friction Materials Power Modern Machinery

paras.en: How Paper-Based Friction Materials Power Modern Machinery

Have you ever wondered what enables everything from roaring construction machinery to agricultural machinery plowing the fields to industrial equipment shuttling through factories—the precise starting, smooth operation, and reliable braking they achieve?

The answer lies in a seemingly insignificant yet crucial core component: friction material. It acts as the "safety guard" and "power link" of machinery, ensuring every brake is safe and effective, and every power transmission is smooth and flawless.

Among the vast family of friction materials, wet friction materials are becoming the new favorite in modern machinery due to their exceptional reliability, safety, and exceptionally long lifespan. Among wet materials, paper-based friction materials stand out as a leading force thanks to their excellent overall performance, cost-effectiveness, and broad application prospects.
Today, let's delve deeper into the fascinating world of this "unsung hero"—paper-based friction materials.
What is Paper-Based Friction Material? — A Sponge-Like Power Core
Imagine a "sponge" with countless tiny pores—that's the most intuitive image of paper-based friction material.

It is a material with a reticular porous structure composed of three core components: reinforcing fibers, functional fillers, and a binder resin. This unique structure gives it extraordinary capabilities:
- Oil Storage Capacity: The porous structure acts like a miniature "oil depot," capable of storing large quantities of lubricant.

- Dynamic Lubrication: When the friction plate and mating plate engage and are subjected to pressure, the lubricant within the material is instantly squeezed onto the friction surface, forming a tough lubricant film, enabling smooth, gentle "wet" friction.
- Self-Recovery: When the friction plates separate, the material rebounds like memory foam, "absorbing" the lubricant back into the pores, ready for the next operation.

It is this dynamic cycle of "oil storage-oil squeezing-oil return" that allows paper-based friction materials to perform well in an oil bath environment, achieving a perfect combination of high durability and stable friction performance.
Exploring Core Performance: How Do Three Key Factors Affect It?

The performance of paper-based friction materials is not static. Like a top athlete, its performance is influenced by the "field," "equipment," and "condition." Let's examine how these three key factors shape its performance.
Factor 1: The "Stage Effect" of Lubricants

Paper-based friction materials are highly sensitive to lubricants, and different lubricants create distinct "stages" for their performance. Even the same friction material can exhibit significantly different friction characteristics (especially the kinetic friction coefficient) when exposed to different lubricants.
Figure 1: Kinetic friction coefficient curve for a paper-based friction material in gear oil
Figure 2: Dynamic friction coefficient curve of the same material in hydraulic oil

Interpretation: The above chart clearly shows that the same material behaves very differently in gear oil and hydraulic fluid. Furthermore, various additives added to lubricating oils (such as dispersants and anti-wear agents) can interact complexly with the material surface, further affecting its friction properties. Therefore, choosing the right oil for paper-based friction materials is the first step in achieving optimal performance.
Density is a trump card for paper-based friction materials. It is directly related to the material's porosity, leading to a delicate balancing act in terms of performance.

High density (low porosity) means a denser material, resulting in better strength and thermal conductivity, lower wear rate, and longer life. However, the downside is reduced oil storage capacity, which can lead to a lower coefficient of friction and compromise power transmission.

Low density (high porosity) means the material is more porous, resulting in greater oil storage capacity and a higher coefficient of friction, which can provide greater braking force or transmit torque. However, the downside is reduced mechanical strength and wear resistance, shortening service life.
Figure 3: Comparison of the dynamic coefficient of friction for materials of varying densities (Type 2 to Type 6, increasing density)
Figure 4: Comparison of wear rates of materials with different densities

Interpretation: Figures 3 and 4 vividly illustrate this balancing act. There's no such thing as absolute good or bad, only suitability. When selecting a paper-based friction material, the optimal trade-off between friction coefficient and durability must be determined based on specific application requirements (e.g., high torque versus long life).
Factor 3: Extreme Challenges of Operating Conditions

In addition to oil type and density, actual operating conditions, such as surface pressure, sliding speed, and oil temperature, pose extreme challenges to paper-based friction materials. These factors directly affect the temperature of the friction interface, the thickness and stability of the oil film, and thus dynamically alter the coefficient of friction.

Therefore, please remember: the coefficient of friction of a particular paper-based friction material is not a fixed value, but rather a performance range determined through extensive and repeated testing under specific operating conditions.
Broad Applications: Injecting a Powerful "Heart" into Machinery
