paras.zh: 康沃利斯号并不是游牧探险队成功定位的第一艘沉船。 2017 年，他们发现了 SS William H. Machen 号货船，这是一艘 1942 年在朴茨茅斯海岸沉没的货船。一年后，他们找到了 USS Eagle 56，这是一艘于 1945 年 4 月在缅因州伊丽莎白角附近被德国鱼雷击沉的军舰。

paras.en: They decided to go after the Cornwallis because it was the largest missing vessel in all of New England. They were also intrigued by the ship’s history. Two years before it sank off the coast of Maine, the ship was torpedoed by a German U-boat while sailing in Barbados. It partially sank, but was refloated, repaired and returned to service. It’s one of just five ships known to have been torpedoed and sunk twice, per the Halifax Chronicle Herald’s Ian Fairclough.
paras.zh: 他们决定追捕康沃利斯号，因为它是新英格兰地区最大的失踪船只。他们也对这艘船的历史感兴趣。在缅因州海岸沉没的两年前，这艘船在巴巴多斯航行时被一艘德国潜艇的鱼雷击中。它部分沉没，但被重新浮起、修复并恢复使用。据《哈利法克斯纪事先驱报》的伊恩·费尔克拉夫报道，这是已知两次被鱼雷击沉的五艘船之一。

paras.en: According to the divers, the wreck is located in federal waters. The state of Maine can’t claim ownership of it, nor can the U.S. Navy, meaning it “belongs to everyone and no one,” Allan explains to the Bangor Daily News.
paras.zh: 据潜水员称，沉船位于联邦水域。艾伦向《班戈每日新闻》解释说，缅因州不能声称拥有它，美国海军也不能，这意味着它“属于所有人，而不属于任何人”。

paras.en: “We could file paperwork to take ownership of it, [but] we’re not planning to do that,” he adds. “For us, the real reward is to find the wreck, put a place on the map [and] give closure to the families.”
paras.zh: “我们可以提交文件来获得它的所有权，但我们不打算这样做，”他补充道。 “对我们来说，真正的奖励是找到残骸，在地图上找到一个地方，[并]为遇难者家属提供一个解脱。”

paras.en: The team also hopes the discovery shines a light on how close the war came to the shores of New England. Though it wasn’t a military vessel, the Cornwallis was equipped with machine guns and had seven armed guards on board when it sank.
paras.zh: 研究小组还希望这一发现能让人们了解战争距离新英格兰海岸有多近。尽管它不是军舰，但康沃利斯号沉没时配备了机枪，船上还有七名武装警卫。

paras.en: Looking ahead, the divers plan to return to the wreck site and continue exploring it using a remotely operated underwater vehicle. They’ve also identified their next target, Allan tells the Portsmouth Herald. He wouldn’t share the name of the vessel, revealing only that it's a “very large wreck, several hundred feet long [that] went down with all hands on deck.”
paras.zh: 展望未来，潜水员计划返回沉船现场，并使用遥控水下航行器继续探索。艾伦告诉朴茨茅斯先驱报，他们还确定了下一个目标。他不愿透露这艘船的名称，只透露这是一艘“非常大的残骸，有数百英尺长，甲板上的所有人都在沉没”。

articles.title: How Elon Musk and Big Tech Poured Millions Into the Midterms, and Lost
articles.author: Leah Feiger, Hugo Lowell, Vittoria Elliott, David Gilbert

paras.en: This week on Uncanny Valley, Hugo Lowell, David Gilbert, and Vittoria Elliott from WIRED’s politics team join Leah Feiger to break down how Democrats flipped both the House and the Senate, and why the MAGA base is pinning the losses on Trump and the Iran war. We look at how more than $400 million from Elon Musk’s super PAC largely came up empty, why voters restricted 39 of 40 data center ballot measures in what WIRED called the data center referendum, why election deniers suddenly went quiet, and what it all means for 2028.
paras.zh: 本周，在《恐怖谷》节目中，《连线》政治团队的雨果·洛厄尔、大卫·吉尔伯特和维多利亚·埃利奥特与利亚·费格一起剖析了民主党是如何颠覆众议院和参议院的，以及为什么“让美国再次伟大”基地将损失归咎于特朗普和伊朗战争。我们来看看埃隆·马斯克的超级政治行动委员会的 4 亿多美元是如何大部分落空的，为什么选民在《连线》杂志所谓的数据中心公投中限制了 40 项数据中心投票措施中的 39 项，为什么选举否认者突然安静下来，以及这一切对 2028 年意味着什么。

paras.en: You can follow Leah Feiger on Bluesky at @leahfeiger, Hugo Lowell on Bluesky at @hugolowell, David Gilbert on Bluesky at @davidgilbert, and Vittoria Elliott on Bluesky at @telliotter. Write to us at [email protected].
paras.zh: 您可以通过 @leahfeiger 关注 Bluesky 的 Leah Feiger、@hugolowell 关注 Hugo Lowell 的 Bluesky、@davidgilbert 关注 David Gilbert 的 Bluesky，以及 @telliotter 关注 Vittoria Elliott 的 Bluesky。请通过 [email protected] 给我们写信。

paras.en: If you're on an iPhone or iPad, open the app called Podcasts, or just tap this link. You can also download an app like Overcast or Pocket Casts and search for “uncanny valley.” We’re on Spotify too.
paras.zh: 如果您使用的是 iPhone 或 iPad，请打开名为“播客”的应用程序，或者只需点击此链接。您还可以下载 Overcast 或 Pocket Casts 等应用程序，然后搜索“恐怖谷”。我们也在 Spotify 上。

paras.en: Note: This is an automated transcript, which may contain errors.
paras.zh: 注意：这是一个自动记录，可能包含错误。

paras.en: Brian Barrett: Welcome to WIRED's Uncanny Valley. I'm Brian Barrett, executive editor.
paras.zh: 布莱恩·巴雷特：欢迎来到《连线》的恐怖谷。我是布赖恩·巴雷特，执行主编。

paras.en: Zoë Schiffer: I'm Zoë Schiffer, contributing editor.
paras.zh: Zoë Schiffer：我是 Zoë Schiffer，特约编辑。

paras.en: Leah Feiger: Not this week, folks. Sorry, Zoë and Brian. The midterms have just wrapped up and the politics team is taking over the feed. Welcome to WIRED's Uncanny Valley. I am Leah Feiger, director of politics and science. This week we're bringing you a special midterms episode. I'm joined by three of my WIRED colleagues, Hugo Lowell, a senior correspondent covering the Trump White House.
paras.zh: Leah Feiger：伙计们，本周不行。抱歉，佐伊和布莱恩。中期选举刚刚结束，政治团队正在接管一切。欢迎来到《连线》的恐怖谷。我是莉亚·费格 (Leah Feiger)，政治和科学部主任。本周我们将为您带来特别的期中考试节目。我的三位《连线》同事雨果·洛厄尔（Hugo Lowell）也加入了我的行列，他是一位报道特朗普白宫的高级记者。

paras.en: Leah Feiger: David Gilbert, senior reporter who focuses on disinformation and extremism.
paras.zh: Leah Feiger：大卫·吉尔伯特，资深记者，专注于虚假信息和极端主义。

paras.en: Leah Feiger: And senior writer Vittoria Elliott, who focuses on the internal machinations of the US government.
paras.zh: 利亚·费格：还有资深作家维多利亚·埃利奥特，她专注于美国政府的内部阴谋。

paras.en: Vittoria Elliott: Good to be here, Leah.
paras.zh: 维多利亚·埃利奥特：很高兴来到这里，利亚。

paras.en: Leah Feiger: We'll get into how these candidates supported by Elon Musk and AI super PACs ended up faring and why these elections were rebuked by Americans of not just the current government, but also of Big Tech. So the Democrats needed a net gain of four seats in the Senate and three in the House. They blew by both. What were your biggest shocks of the evening, everyone?
paras.zh: Leah Feiger：我们将探讨埃隆·马斯克和人工智能超级政治行动委员会支持的这些候选人最终的表现，以及为什么这些选举不仅受到美国人的谴责，不仅包括现任政府，还包括大型科技公司。因此，民主党需要在参议院净增加四个席位，在众议院净增加三个席位。他们都被击败了。大家今晚最大的震惊是什么？

paras.en: David Gilbert: Well, because I am based in Ireland, I woke up on Wednesday morning and the landscape had just completely changed. Even people who were in deep red states like Arizona, like Mark Lamb, who was a certainty to win, his race still hasn't been drawn. It's just exceptional.
paras.zh: 大卫·吉尔伯特：嗯，因为我住在爱尔兰，所以我在周三早上醒来，发现风景完全改变了。即使是亚利桑那州等深红州的人，比如马克·兰姆(Mark Lamb)，他肯定会获胜，但他的竞选仍然没有分出胜负。这真是太棒了。

paras.en: Vittoria Elliott: I was floored by how tight Mississippi is and the win in South Carolina. I would not have put my money on that. Incredible.
paras.zh: 维多利亚·埃利奥特（Vittoria Elliott）：密西西比州的紧张局势和南卡罗来纳州的胜利让我感到震惊。我不会把钱花在这上面。极好的。

paras.en: Hugo Lowell: Yeah, I agree with Tori. South Carolina, Darline Graham was handpicked by Trump and endorsed by him to win that race. And it was not this close in previous cycles.
paras.zh: 雨果·洛厄尔：是的，我同意托里的观点。南卡罗来纳州的达林·格雷厄姆 (Darline Graham) 是特朗普精心挑选并支持赢得那场竞选的。在之前的周期中，情况并没有这么接近。

paras.en: Leah Feiger: To inherit her brother's seat.
paras.zh: Leah Feiger：继承她哥哥的席位。

paras.en: Hugo Lowell: Insane. And she ended up losing it. And then also in Mississippi, the fact that Cindy Hyde-Smith, who's been in the Senate a long time, was once considered to be a very, very safe incumbent losing in deep red Mississippi. I mean, it's not been called yet, but that was also a massive shock. And I think what really stood out to me was having been at Trump's election night party in 2024 for that presidential run and how everyone there was talking about how Trump had put together this historic coalition, was making big gains in all sorts of places where they didn't expect to and took all of the battleground states. What happened on Tuesday night, on election night was a reversal of all of those gains and then some. I mean, if you think about Trump winning double digits in battleground states and then seeing what happened on Tuesday, those states swung 10 points back in the other direction for Democrats. And it just, I think, goes to show how in 18 months and 20 months, Trump has managed to undo everything and all of the goodwill that Republicans have built up in the '24 election cycle through all of his vanity projects, all of the cuts with DOGE, all of his acts in the federal government, and really the fact that he led the country into an unpopular war that led to higher prices, which are even more unpopular.
paras.zh: 雨果·洛厄尔：疯了。而她最终还是失去了它。还有在密西西比州，长期担任参议院议员的辛迪·海德·史密斯（Cindy Hyde-Smith）曾经被认为是深红色密西西比州非常非常安全的现任议员。我的意思是，它还没有被调用，但这也是一个巨大的震惊。我认为真正让我印象深刻的是，我参加了 2024 年特朗普竞选总统的选举之夜派对，那里的每个人都在谈论特朗普如何组建了这个历史性的联盟，在他们意想不到的各种地方取得了巨大进展，并占领了所有战场州。周二晚上，选举之夜发生的事情是所有这些成果的逆转，然后是一些。我的意思是，如果你想想特朗普在摇摆州赢得了两位数的胜利，然后看看周二发生的事情，这些州的支持率就向民主党的另一个方向倒退了 10 个百分点。我认为，这只是表明，特朗普如何在 18 个月和 20 个月的时间里，通过他所有的虚荣项目、所有与 DOGE 的削减、他在联邦政府中的所有行为，以及他带领国家陷入一场不受欢迎的战争，导致物价上涨，而事实上他带领国家陷入了一场不受欢迎的战争，导致物价上涨，而这实际上是更不受欢迎的事实，他成功地毁掉了共和党人在 24 年选举周期中建立起来的一切和所有善意。

paras.en: Leah Feiger: Absolutely. I mean, I was messaging with Democrats on Tuesday night who were telling me that they really couldn't have, in their wildest dreams, thought that this was going to happen. It wasn't like just picking up Maine or just picking up South Carolina. It was Maine, North Carolina, Ohio, Texas, Iowa, Kansas, South Carolina, Michigan. And obviously for Republicans, the blame game has started. This was an unpopular president leading an unpopular war with a variety of, as you mentioned, policies that really hit home for a lot of Americans and residents. So Trump, after the election, blamed the quality of the candidates and the fact that he wasn't on the ballot. The MAGA base didn't totally agree. David, you reported out a story about how MAGA basically went feral, I think is the fair way to put it on Tuesday night and Wednesday morning looking at all of the results come in. What did you see?
paras.zh: 利亚·费格：当然。我的意思是，周二晚上我给民主党人发信息，他们告诉我，他们在最疯狂的梦想中真的不可能想到这会发生。这不像只是拿起缅因州或只是拿起南卡罗来纳州。分别是缅因州、北卡罗来纳州、俄亥俄州、德克萨斯州、爱荷华州、堪萨斯州、南卡罗来纳州、密歇根州。显然，对于共和党人来说，指责游戏已经开始。正如你提到的，这是一位不受欢迎的总统，他领导了一场不受欢迎的战争，其政策对许多美国人和居民来说确实击中了要害。因此，特朗普在选举后指责候选人的素质以及他没有参加选票的事实。 MAGA基地并不完全同意。大卫，你报道了一个关于 MAGA 基本上如何变得野性的故事，我认为在周二晚上和周三早上查看所有结果是公平的方式。你看到了什么？

paras.en: David Gilbert: Yeah, it was interesting to look at how it played out because Trump also blamed Fox News, let's not forget, because he said they had a lot to bear because they platformed a lot of Democrats because that's what they do. But I think the first reaction was kind of silenced because a lot of people just could not believe it. If you looked at what Steve Bannon show and they kept bringing up new results in Texas in particular, he just kind of couldn't believe that what he was seeing was actually happening. So I think initially they were just shocked like pretty much everyone else that this was actually happening to the extent that it was happening. But slowly then they began to say, "OK, well, this is because of the war and the war that Trump more particularly got us into." So figures like Matt Walsh, who has been critical of the war for quite a while now, was kind of laying it all out saying, "This is exactly why we've had such a reversal from 2024."
paras.zh: 大卫·吉尔伯特：是的，看看事情的结果很有趣，因为特朗普也指责福克斯新闻，我们不要忘记，因为他说他们要承受很多，因为他们为很多民主党人站台，因为这就是他们所做的。但我认为第一反应有点沉默，因为很多人都不敢相信。如果你看看史蒂夫·班农（Steve Bannon）展示的内容，他们不断提出新的结果，特别是在德克萨斯州，他只是有点不敢相信他所看到的事情真的发生了。所以我认为最初他们只是像其他人一样感到震惊，因为这确实发生了。但慢慢地，他们开始说：“好吧，好吧，这是因为战争，尤其是特朗普让我们卷入的战争。”因此，马特·沃尔什（Matt Walsh）等人物长期以来一直对这场战争持批评态度，他似乎把一切都摆在了面前，他说：“这正是我们从 2024 年开始出现如此逆转的原因。”

paras.en: Leah Feiger: I mean, Walsh, who's an infamous right-wing podcaster, quite literally called Trump, "An 80-year-old lame duck president," and called the results, "A political catastrophe of historic proportions." It doesn't get more official than that. And this for me was the first time that I saw this blame game laid out so concisely, so specifically, and so squarely on Trump's shoulders.
paras.zh: Leah Feiger：我的意思是，沃尔什，一位臭名昭著的右翼播客，毫不夸张地称特朗普为“一位 80 岁的跛脚鸭总统”，并称其结果为“一场历史性的政治灾难”。没有比这更官方的了。对我来说，这是我第一次看到这种指责游戏如此简洁、如此具体、如此明确地落在特朗普的肩上。

paras.en: David Gilbert: Yeah, I think they realized very quickly that they couldn't look anywhere else except at Trump because the pushback or the reaction was so strong that there really wasn't anywhere else to look.
paras.zh: 大卫·吉尔伯特：是的，我认为他们很快意识到，除了特朗普之外，他们不能把目光投向其他任何地方，因为阻力或反应是如此强烈，以至于真的没有其他地方可看。

paras.en: Hugo Lowell: Yeah, I still think it's early, but it is very quick how people coalesced behind blaming Pete Hegseth, for one, the Secretary of Defense, or Secretary of War because of his encouragement of Trump for months and months about continuing the Iran war. He has been a big cheerleader for continuing to have kinetic strikes, for continuing to extend deployments in the Middle East, and being pretty unapologetic about championing the conflict essentially.
paras.zh: 雨果·洛厄尔：是的，我仍然认为现在还为时过早，但人们很快就联合起来指责皮特·赫格斯（Pete Hegseth），例如国防部长或战争部长，因为他几个月来鼓励特朗普继续伊朗战争。他一直是继续发动动能打击、继续扩大在中东的部署以及对本质上支持冲突毫无歉意的大力支持者。

paras.en: Leah Feiger: You had one piece of reporting in there that was absolutely mind-blowing to me, honestly, that Hegseth's reports from the Iran war to the president were so rosy, so glowing that Vice President JD Vance and Marco Rubio from State, they ended up having to ask people for their own intelligence briefings because they were very aware they were not getting an accurate assessment of the war on the ground. That's pretty unbelievable.
paras.zh: 利亚·费格：老实说，你的一篇报道绝对让我震惊，赫格斯向总统提交的伊朗战争报告是如此乐观，如此令人兴奋，副总统 JD 万斯和马可·卢比奥最终不得不向人们索要自己的情报简报，因为他们非常清楚自己没有得到对实地战争的准确评估。这真是令人难以置信。

paras.en: Hugo Lowell: Yeah, I mean look, Rubio and JD Vance have both been very voracious consumers of intelligence products. That was the case even before the Iran war, but our sources tell us that interest in getting an unvarnished somber look at the situation in Iran became a top priority for those guys because at the end of the day, they have their own political ambitions, but they also have to advise the president themselves. And so they felt like they needed to arm themselves with the facts of the matter in order to guide the president in the best way. And this all coalesces, right? It's like the fact that the Iran war was being presented to Trump in such a rosy way meant he felt more emboldened to continue it. People inside the administration thought, "Well, this is actually not the situation." And had Trump been maybe, I want to say misled, but had he received a different characterization, maybe he would've been less interested in continuing the conflict, especially months before the midterms.
paras.zh: 雨果·洛厄尔：是的，我的意思是，卢比奥和 JD 万斯都是情报产品的狂热消费者。甚至在伊朗战争之前就是这种情况，但我们的消息来源告诉我们，对伊朗局势进行不加掩饰的严肃审视成为这些人的首要任务，因为归根结底，他们有自己的政治野心，但他们也必须自己向总统提供建议。因此，他们觉得自己需要用事实武装自己，以便以最好的方式指导总统。这一切都结合在一起，对吗？就像伊朗战争以如此乐观的方式呈现给特朗普这一事实意味着他更有底气继续战争一样。政府内部人士想：“其实情况并非如此。”我想说，如果特朗普可能被误导了，但如果他得到了不同的描述，也许他对继续冲突就不那么感兴趣了，尤其是在中期选举前几个月。

paras.en: Leah Feiger: It's amazing. There's really no other word for it. So let's talk about spending. If we're going to talk about spending, we have to talk about Elon Musk. He spent over $400 million in this midterm cycle, largely attacking Democrats and supporting Republican candidates. He virtually set his money on fire. According to a WIRED analysis, by Wednesday morning, candidates backed by Musk's America PAC had lost 20 races and won only 1. There are still several that haven't been called yet, but to put another way with where we're at right now with the information we have, of every traceable dollar that Musk put into a race that has now been decided, more than 99 cents went to a race that he lost. Just unbelievable figures there.
paras.zh: 利亚·费格：太棒了。真的没有其他词可以形容它。那么我们来谈谈支出吧。如果我们要谈论支出，我们就必须谈论埃隆·马斯克。他在这个中期周期中花费了超过 4 亿美元，主要攻击民主党并支持共和党候选人。他几乎把他的钱都烧了。据《连线》杂志分析，截至周三上午，马斯克的美国政治行动委员会支持的候选人已经输掉了 20 场比赛，只赢得了 1 场。还有几场比赛还没有被召集，但换个角度来看，根据我们目前掌握的信息，马斯克在现已确定的竞选中投入的每一块可追踪的美元中，超过 99 美分都花在了他输掉的比赛上。那里只有令人难以置信的数字。

paras.en: Vittoria Elliott: I mean, I think it's pretty incredible that two years ago, America PAC was this new force in Republican politics. Everyone was starting to play to the sort of America PAC donation situation, and it pulled in not just money from Musk, it pulled in money from big VCs like Shaun Maguire. And in 2024, as we reported, their ground game wasn't exactly super strong, but it was just the willingness to pump money in. Similar to how VCs make things work, you pump money in until your team wins. And just to watch that strategy really crash and burn, but I think we saw some early indications that, particularly in the months post-DOGE, that Elon himself became a really toxic thing for Republicans to start attaching themselves to.
paras.zh: 维多利亚·埃利奥特：我的意思是，我认为两年前美国政治行动委员会成为共和党政治中的新生力量是非常令人难以置信的。每个人都开始利用美国 PAC 的捐款情况，它不仅从马斯克那里吸引资金，还从像肖恩马奎尔这样的大型风险投资公司那里吸引资金。正如我们报道的那样，到了 2024 年，他们的地面游戏并不是非常强大，但这只是愿意注入资金。与风险投资公司让事情发挥作用的方式类似，你注入资金，直到你的团队获胜。只是为了看到这一策略真正崩溃和燃烧，但我认为我们看到了一些早期迹象，特别是在 DOGE 后的几个月里，埃隆本人成为共和党人开始依附的真正有毒的东西。

paras.en: Vittoria Elliott: And so then it became this sort of monkey's paw situation where it's like you can take the America PAC money and then you get tarred with the Musk brand. And those two things, maybe at best they cancel each other out, but it seems like actually the Musk brand is more toxic than he and his candidates could buy their way out of.
paras.zh: 维多利亚·埃利奥特（Vittoria Elliott）：所以这就变成了一种猴爪的情况，就像你可以拿走美国政治行动委员会的钱，然后你就会沾上马斯克的品牌。这两件事，也许充其量是相互抵消的，但实际上，马斯克品牌的毒性似乎比他和他的候选人所能摆脱的还要大。

paras.en: Leah Feiger: I 100 percent agree with you. Hugo, you were very involved in the WIRED tracking project where we built a live tracker of Musk's political spending. Can you take us through a couple of the candidates that he put all of this dough behind and how they ended up doing?
paras.zh: Leah Feiger：我百分百同意你的观点。雨果，你非常参与《连线》跟踪项目，我们在该项目中建立了马斯克政治支出的实时跟踪器。您能否向我们介绍一下他投入所有资金的几位候选人以及他们最终的表现如何？

paras.en: Hugo Lowell: Yeah, look, in total, Musk's America PAC spent about close to $500 million actually, half a billion dollars this midterm cycle, him alone. I mean, if you conceptualize that sort of spending, the way to think about it I think is he effectively ran a shadow Republican national committee. That is the scale of that contribution. And were it not for that money, by the way, some of these losses might've been even greater. Tori talked about the ground game that America PAC financed, that has been a big focus both in '24 and also in this cycle. Obviously his biggest focus was Texas. That is his home base. That was where he spent the most amount of time, the most amount of money and the most amount of resources, and it basically got him nothing. I mean, Ken Paxton lost by such a wide margin that hanging onto James Talarico's coattails was Gina Hinojosa in the governor's race. So I think the way to look at Musk's spending, if you talk to Republican operatives and people in Trump world, is to think about it in terms of what is this money actually buying him? For him, it's a rounding era. Half a billion dollars to Elon, it's kind of pocket change, which is kind of incredible to think about, but that is the case. And so what is the net effect he gets from this? And it is probably the fact that he can play kingmaker now running into 2028. And if he decides to back a particular presidential candidate, I'm sorry to say this, we already just finished this election, but '28 is around the corner. If he decides to back a particular candidate, no one else is really going to be able to compete with him on the money front because if he sinks another half billion, if not more, in the next cycle, who else has that kind of money to play with? It's insane.
paras.zh: 雨果·洛厄尔：是的，看看，马斯克的美国政治行动委员会实际上总共花费了近 5 亿美元，在这个中期周期中，仅他一个人就花费了 5 亿美元。我的意思是，如果你将这种支出概念化，我认为思考它的方式是他实际上管理着一个影子共和党全国委员会。这就是贡献的规模。顺便说一句，如果没有这笔钱，其中一些损失可能会更大。 Tori 谈到了 America PAC 资助的地面游戏，这一直是 24 年以及本周期的一大焦点。显然他最关注的焦点是德克萨斯州。那是他的大本营。那是他花费最多时间、最多金钱、最多资源的地方，但基本上什么也没得到。我的意思是，肯·帕克斯顿（Ken Paxton）以如此大的差距落败，以至于吉娜·伊诺霍萨（Gina Hinojosa）在州长竞选中紧随詹姆斯·塔拉里科（James Talarico）的脚步。因此，我认为，如果你与共和党工作人员和特朗普世界的人们交谈，看待马斯克支出的方法就是思考这些钱实际上给他买了什么？对于他来说，这是一个轮回的时代。对于埃隆来说，这 5 亿美元只是一笔零花钱，这对他来说有点难以置信。 想一想，也不过如此。那么他从中得到的最终效果是什么呢？事实上，他现在可以扮演造王者的角色，直到 2028 年。如果他决定支持某个特定的总统候选人，我很遗憾地说，我们刚刚结束了这次选举，但 28 年即将到来。如果他决定支持某个特定候选人，那么没有其他人真正能够在金钱方面与他竞争，因为如果他在下一个周期再损失五亿美元，甚至更多，那么还有谁有那么多钱可以玩呢？太疯狂了。

paras.en: Leah Feiger: But I think the takeaway, at least in this moment, is that money didn't matter. He couldn't buy these races. People were so mad at Republicans and so mad at Trump's mandate that this didn't actually work out for him. I'm not sure, going into 2028, I would necessarily want Elon Musk behind me.
paras.zh: Leah Feiger：但我认为，至少在此刻，钱并不重要。他买不到这些比赛。人们对共和党人和特朗普的授权非常生气，以至于这对他来说实际上并没有成功。我不确定，进入 2028 年，我是否一定希望埃隆·马斯克在我身后。

paras.en: Hugo Lowell: I don't know that voters necessarily see that, though, right? I mean, are voters really tracking which ad was paid for by which super PAC? I understand that the money didn't buy a Texas Senate race. By the way, as it shouldn't, this concept that you can just buy Senate races. And I take your point and I see what you're saying, but it is not clear to me that whether the money would've come from the Senate leadership fund, which is the super PAC aligned with the Senate Republican leadership, or whether it came from America PAC, in some ways doesn't matter. It's like the volume of cash that flowed in, where is that going to be going, and what does the future of those kinds of contributions look like? And I do think it kind of flows into '28.
paras.zh: 雨果·洛厄尔：我不知道选民一定会看到这一点，对吧？我的意思是，选民是否真的追踪哪个超级政治行动委员会支付了哪个广告费用？我知道这笔钱并没有买到德克萨斯州参议员竞选。顺便说一句，这是不应该的，这个概念是你可以购买参议院竞选。我同意你的观点，我明白你在说什么，但我不清楚这笔钱是来自参议院领导基金（与参议院共和党领导层结盟的超级政治行动委员会），还是来自美国政治行动委员会，在某些方面并不重要。这就像流入的现金量，将流向哪里，以及这些捐款的未来会是什么样子？我确实认为它会流入 28 年。

paras.en: Vittoria Elliott: I would just argue that yeah, maybe if he wrapped the money on many, many layers of PACs that made it hard to trace where it came from, I would agree with you. But anyone who gets money that flows from Elon or even his association with the party allows for someone to run an attack ad that says, "Elon backs this guy. Elon backs this party." They're going to execute on the unpopular will of an unelected billionaire, I think is still going to be toxic even if the money eventually gets routed through the general Republican funding apparatus.
paras.zh: Vittoria Elliott：我只是想说，是的，也许如果他把钱包装在很多很多层的 PAC 上，这样就很难追踪它的来源，我会同意你的观点。但任何从埃隆那里获得资金的人，甚至是他与该党的关系，都允许有人发布攻击性广告，上面写着：“埃隆支持这个人。埃隆支持这个政党。”他们将按照一位未经选举的亿万富翁不受欢迎的意愿来执行，我认为即使这笔钱最终通过共和党的一般资助机构，这仍然是有毒的。

paras.en: Leah Feiger: I think the thought that this is in some ways all a preview for '28 is the right take. Sort of in that vein is where the AI industry showed up in this election cycle as well. Leading the future, which is the pro-AI network backed by Andreessen Horowitz and OpenAI president Greg Brockman, among others. They threw in money for Republican primaries, Democratic ones. They've been sort of all over the place. And to me, and to some of the experts people on our team have spoken to, that's really spelled out that they're just kind of laying the groundwork for '28. They want to see where different, not just races, land but where the population is landing on all of these different issues, which I guess takes us to data centers, a topic that I did not think was going to consume 2026 for me, but here we are. Tori, we have been framing this election quite a lot as the data center referendum. We were not wrong. Across the country, there were 40 ballot measures about AI data center projects. Voters chose to restrict 39 of them, and an NBC exit poll found that almost a quarter of all voters said that data centers were crucial to their vote. Absolutely mind-boggling. Voters hated AI. Voters hated data centers. Talk to us about what you and science senior reporter Molly Taft reported out for WIRED.
paras.zh: Leah Feiger：我认为认为这在某种程度上是 28 年的预览是正确的。人工智能行业在本次选举周期中也出现了类似的情况。引领未来的是由 Andreessen Horowitz 和 OpenAI 总裁 Greg Brockman 等人支持的亲人工智能网络。他们为共和党初选、民主党初选投入资金。他们几乎到处都是。对我以及我们团队中的一些专家来说，这确实表明他们只是为 28 岁月奠定基础。他们想了解不同的人（不仅仅是种族）在所有这些不同的问题上登陆在哪里，而且人口在哪里登陆，我想这将我们带到数据中心，我认为这个话题不会消耗我 2026 年的时间，但我们在这里。 Tori，我们一直将这次选举视为数据中心公投。我们没有错。全国范围内，有40项关于人工智能数据中心项目的投票措施。选民选择限制其中的 39 个，NBC 的出口民意调查发现，近四分之一的选民表示数据中心对他们的投票至关重要。绝对令人难以置信。选民讨厌人工智能。选民讨厌数据中心。与我们谈谈您和科学高级记者莫莉·塔夫脱 (Molly Taft) 为《连线》杂志报道的内容。

paras.en: Vittoria Elliott: Yeah, so I think a couple of things. First off, I think this sort of ties in many ways to people's resentment of the tech industry and its rightward swing more generally, and data centers and AI are sort of the peak embodiment of that. And obviously there's the environmental concerns around data centers, and I think you really saw it as a galvanizing force in rural communities where these data centers are being put, where in communities that really would've more traditionally swung Republican, that it became this really bipartisan uniting effort around the fact that—
paras.zh: 维多利亚·埃利奥特：是的，所以我想了几件事。首先，我认为这在很多方面与人们对科技行业及其更普遍的右倾的不满情绪有关，而数据中心和人工智能就是这种情绪的巅峰体现。显然，数据中心存在环境问题，我认为您确实将其视为这些数据中心所在农村社区的一股激励力量，在那些传统上更倾向于共和党的社区，它成为真正的两党团结努力，围绕以下事实：

paras.en: Leah Feiger: I can't think of another issue, honestly, that has galvanized.
paras.zh: Leah Feiger：说实话，我想不出还有哪个问题引起了人们的关注。

paras.en: Vittoria Elliott: I know, something we can all agree on.
paras.zh: 维多利亚·埃利奥特：我知道，这是我们都同意的。

paras.en: Vittoria Elliott: So to go back to South Carolina, for instance, Darline Graham got dubbed Data Center Darline because she was taking money from data center PACs. In Montana with Sam Forstag, a Democratic up-and-comer, fire jumper—his opponent also tarred and feathered with the data center label in a historically Republican district. So I think we are really seeing this moment where these things are touching down in communities that normally would be Republican, and they're seeing these impacts on their daily lives and having Republican representatives-
paras.zh: Vittoria Elliott：例如，回到南卡罗来纳州，Darline Graham 被称为“数据中心 Darline”，因为她从数据中心 PAC 获取资金。在蒙大拿州，民主党后起之秀萨姆·福斯塔格 (Sam Forstag) 跳火，他的对手也在一个历史悠久的共和党选区涂上了柏油并贴上了数据中心的标签。因此，我认为我们确实看到了这些事情在通常属于共和党的社区中落地的时刻，他们看到了这些对他们日常生活的影响，并拥有了共和党代表——

paras.en: Leah Feiger: Or even just the threat of the impact on their daily lives. People were running on, "There could be a data center in your community. Don't worry, I'll stop it from happening." That was Chris Pappas in New Hampshire, for example.
paras.zh: Leah Feiger：或者甚至只是对他们日常生活影响的威胁。人们纷纷议论，“你们的社区里可能有一个数据中心。别担心，我会阻止它发生。”例如，他就是新罕布什尔州的克里斯·帕帕斯。

paras.en: Vittoria Elliott: Totally. And especially in places like Georgia and Texas where a lot of these things are already up and running or are planned, resounding, resounding population telling Republican lawmakers to step off with that. They're not interested. Telling people, "We're going to put this thing in your community. It's going to take up your water. It's going to be loud. It's going to be annoying. It's going to be expensive. It's going to drive up your electricity bills in the middle of an affordability crisis." And then saying to them, "And reward for all of that is it's going to take your job in the middle of a jobs crisis where tons and tons of people are struggling to find work." I just don't think that's a good selling point. And there were individual Republicans who ran saying that they wanted to regulate the AI industry, that they wanted to push back on data centers, but for the Democrats, it really became sort of a whole party movement around this. And I think that really was rewarded at the ballot box.
paras.zh: 维多利亚·埃利奥特：完全可以。尤其是在佐治亚州和德克萨斯州这样的地方，很多此类事情已经启动并正在运行或正在计划中，人们强烈要求共和党立法者停止这样做。他们不感兴趣。告诉人们，“我们要把这个东西放在你的社区。它会占用你的水。它会很吵。它会很烦人。它会很昂贵。它会在负担能力危机中增加你的电费。”然后对他们说，“所有这一切的回报是，在就业危机中，成千上万的人正在努力寻找工作，这将取代你的工作。”我只是认为这不是一个好的卖点。有个别共和党人在竞选中表示，他们想要监管人工智能行业，他们想要阻止数据中心，但对于民主党来说，这确实成为了围绕这一问题的全党运动。我认为这确实在投票箱中得到了回报。

paras.en: Leah Feiger: Yeah. I mean, there were people who brought it into their victory speeches. Jon Ossoff, when he won his Senate race in Georgia, used his victory speech to specifically call out Silicon Valley titans who build bunkers and warned that their AI could cause human extinction. It was pretty incredible to witness. This is a rallying cry, but I wonder if it's going to be still a rallying cry in two years from now. Let's talk about the people who were very, very convinced that no matter what happened this election cycle, it was all going to be fraud. David, you reported out a story on Wednesday about how all of these election deniers who are usually the very, very first to say that something was wrong, that results were inaccurate, there has to be a recount, there has to be investigations, had nothing to say. Election deniers accepted the results. Talk to us about that.
paras.zh: 利亚·费格：是的。我的意思是，有人把它带入了他们的胜利演讲中。乔恩·奥索夫(Jon Ossoff)在佐治亚州参议员竞选中获胜时，在胜利演讲中特别点名了建造掩体的硅谷巨头，并警告说他们的人工智能可能会导致人类灭绝。亲眼目睹真是令人难以置信。这是一个战斗口号，但我想知道两年后它是否仍然是一个战斗口号。让我们谈谈那些非常非常确信无论这个选举周期发生什么，都将是欺诈的人。大卫，你周三报道了一个故事，内容是所有这些选举否认者通常是最先说有问题、结果不准确、必须重新计票、必须进行调查的人，却无话可说。选举否认者接受了结果。和我们谈谈这个。

paras.en: David Gilbert: Yeah. As I was saying earlier, the MAGA crowd, their first reaction was silence, and then they started the recriminations. But for election deniers, the silence has continued. There was hundreds of election deniers on the ballots, people who had backed Trump's claims that 2020 was a stolen election. Lots of those races still haven't been called. Some of them have won, but lots of them in their most consequential races have lost. People like Andy Biggs, who was running for governor in Arizona, or Mike Rogers, who was running for Senate seat in Michigan—they both had backed Trump's calls in the wake of 2020 to overturn elections. Jim Marchant was running for Secretary of State in Nevada, who was kind of one of the OG election deniers, and he got beaten easily by Cisco Aguilar, who's the incumbent there. But it was just incredible to see when they were making their concession speeches that they didn't mention elections or security or vote rigging or election fraud whatsoever. They didn't mention noncitizens.
paras.zh: 大卫·吉尔伯特：是的。正如我之前所说，MAGA人群，他们的第一反应是沉默，然后他们开始相互指责。但对于否认选举的人来说，沉默仍在继续。选票上有数百名选举否认者，他们支持特朗普关于 2020 年选举被盗的说法。许多比赛还没有被宣布。他们中的一些人赢了，但他们中的许多人在最重要的比赛中失败了。像竞选亚利桑那州州长的安迪·比格斯（Andy Biggs）或竞选密歇根州参议员席位的迈克·罗杰斯（Mike Rogers）这样的人——他们都支持特朗普在 2020 年之后推翻选举的呼吁。吉姆·马钱特 (Jim Marchant) 正在竞选内华达州国务卿，他是 OG 选举的否认者之一，他轻松地被现任内华达州国务卿思科·阿吉拉尔 (Cisco Aguilar) 击败。但令人难以置信的是，当他们发表败选演讲时，他们没有提到选举、安全、操纵选票或选举舞弊等问题。他们没有提到非公民。

paras.en: Leah Feiger: All of your favorite buzzwords.
paras.zh: Leah Feiger：所有你最喜欢的流行语。

paras.en: David Gilbert: Yeah, they mentioned none of them because in most of the cases, the margins of defeat were so great that it just made no sense. But equally, the groups who are kind of backing this movement, the groups like Cleta Mitchell's Election Integrity Network, True to Vote, people like Patrick Byrne, who's funded much of this, they've just been silent, which makes me wonder, is this kind of the beginning of the end of that movement? Have we seen it better out that they've just realized now that, "No, these elections are secure, it's just people really don't like what Trump is doing and the policies that he has?"
paras.zh: 大卫·吉尔伯特：是的，他们没有提到任何一个，因为在大多数情况下，失败的幅度是如此之大，以至于毫无意义。但同样，那些支持这场运动的团体，比如克莱塔·米切尔的选举诚信网络、忠实投票等团体，以及像帕特里克·伯恩这样的人，他们为这场运动提供了大部分资金，他们只是保持沉默，这让我想知道，这是这场运动结束的开始吗？我们是否能更好地看到他们现在刚刚意识到，“不，这些选举是安全的，只是人们真的不喜欢特朗普正在做的事情和他的政策？”

paras.en: Leah Feiger: Something that you had flagged a number of times in the lead-up to the midterms was there were a number of election-denier candidates running for attorney general races in states across the country and Secretary of State races. And those two positions don't tend to get a lot of attention, but they're really important because they have to do with how elections are run in those particular states, which would mean that 2028, the next large election coming up, could have been very well impacted had these candidates won their races. So there is this weird stopping point. Does it feel like the end of an era for you, David?
paras.zh: 利亚·费格：您在中期选举前多次指出的事情是，有许多否认选举的候选人参加全国各州的总检察长竞选和国务卿竞选。这两个职位往往不会引起太多关注，但它们确实很重要，因为它们与这些特定州的选举方式有关，这意味着如果这些候选人赢得竞选，2028 年即将到来的下一次大型选举可能会受到很大影响。所以就有了这个奇怪的停止点。大卫，对你来说这感觉像是一个时代的结束吗？

paras.en: David Gilbert: Well, look, I think we probably are talking about it too early because I think in 2024 we thought that maybe it was over because Trump had won so convincingly, so there was nothing for them to complain about and Trump himself didn't bring it up. But we saw that they came back very quickly again, and there was still a lot of money to be made for a lot of these groups because, for a lot of people involved in this, it is a grift. They were making money; they were traveling across the country talking to people and getting paid for it. I do think based on the initial response that we've seen that lots of the people who were involved in this are tired. Some of the comments I was reading in some of the Telegram channels that I follow are people are just so tired of this, and they seem like they no longer want to take part in it. So it's too early to say that this is the end, but it is possible that a lot of the energy that has been in this movement for six years now will dissipate.
paras.zh: 大卫·吉尔伯特：嗯，看，我认为我们谈论这个问题可能为时过早，因为我认为到 2024 年，我们认为也许一切都结束了，因为特朗普赢得得如此令人信服，所以他们没有什么可抱怨的，特朗普本人也没有提出这个问题。但我们看到他们很快又回来了，而且对于很多这样的团体来说，仍然有很多钱可以赚，因为对于很多参与其中的人来说，这是一种欺骗。他们正在赚钱；他们在全国各地与人们交谈并因此获得报酬。我确实认为，根据我们看到的最初反应，很多参与此事的人都很累。我在我关注的一些 Telegram 频道中读到的一些评论是，人们对此感到非常厌倦，他们似乎不再想参与其中。所以现在说结束还为时过早，但这场运动六年来的大量能量可能会消散。

paras.en: Hugo Lowell: I'm just curious, David, to what extent do you think a lot of this is also follow the leader and the moment Trump came out pretty early on in election night and was like, "I'm going to accept the results." The rest of them thought, "OK, well, if we're not going to have our champion, we're going to stand down too."
paras.zh: 雨果·洛厄尔：我只是很好奇，大卫，你认为这在多大程度上也是追随领导人的，而特朗普在选举之夜很早就出来了，他说，“我要接受结果。”其他人想，“好吧，好吧，如果我们没有冠军，我们也会退出。”

paras.en: David Gilbert: Yeah, I think that's a huge amount to do with it. He hasn't been as active in terms of getting involved in the nitty-gritty of this. He's been making claims that elections are rigged, but I think the movement was kind of self-sustaining, especially in 2025 after Trump had won. So they were able to sustain themselves in that period even when he wasn't promoting them. I do think the fact, though, that he has so quickly accepted defeats in these midterms and hasn't pushed back, I do think that's going to be a big issue for them and will be difficult for them to kind of get themselves motivated once again.
paras.zh: 大卫·吉尔伯特：是的，我认为这与此有很大关系。他并没有那么积极地参与此事的实质内容。他一直声称选举被操纵，但我认为这场运动是一种自我维持，特别是在特朗普获胜后的 2025 年。因此，即使他没有提拔他们，他们也能够在那个时期维持下去。不过，我确实认为，事实上，他很快就接受了中期选举的失败，并且没有反击，我确实认为这对他们来说将是一个大问题，并且他们很难再次激励自己。

paras.en: Leah Feiger: You guys, I want to talk predictions. Midterms, they're over. They're behind us. In January, we're going to have a whole new set of politicians on Capitol Hill, which means it is time to talk about the presidentials. There's a bunch of names that are already floating around: Jon Ossoff, AOC, Gavin Newsom, JD Vance, Marco Rubio. I'm curious what you think. What are your predictions here? What's going to happen? What should we be looking out for in the next few months?
paras.zh: Leah Feiger：各位，我想谈谈预测。期中考试，结束了。他们就在我们身后。一月份，我们将在国会山迎来一批全新的政客，这意味着是时候谈论总统了。有很多名字已经流传开来：Jon Ossoff、AOC、Gavin Newsom、JD Vance、Marco Rubio。我很好奇你怎么想。您对此有何预测？将会发生什么？未来几个月我们应该注意什么？

paras.en: Vittoria Elliott: I mean, I think one of the big things that we saw a lot of Democrats saying immediately last night was subpoena, subpoena, subpoenas, favorite word. And I think unfortunately that's going to run up against some real friction because as Congress, you can subpoena people, you can try and get them to testify, but ultimately all those federal agencies are under the executive branch. They have political leadership now under the Trump administration that is pretty hostile to Congress. And if you want to enforce that subpoena, you are going to need the DOJ to do that for you. And I can't see AG [Todd] Blanche super excited to assist in that. So I think as much as a lot of these Democrats are coming in saying, "We're ready to do accountability," and I do think they want to, I think the actual mechanisms through which they're going to be able to do that are going to be pretty narrowed, and that's something that they're probably going to have to get ahead of explaining to their constituents right now.
paras.zh: 维多利亚·埃利奥特：我的意思是，我认为昨晚我们看到很多民主党人立即说的一件大事就是传票，传票，传票，最喜欢的词。我认为不幸的是，这将遇到一些真正的摩擦，因为作为国会，你可以传唤人们，你可以尝试让他们作证，但最终所有这些联邦机构都在行政部门之下。他们现在在特朗普政府的领导下拥有对国会相当敌视的政治领导层。如果您想执行该传票，您将需要司法部为您执行此操作。我看不出 AG [Todd] Blanche 非常兴奋地协助此事。因此，我认为，尽管很多民主党人都在说，“我们已经准备好问责”，而且我确实认为他们愿意这样做，但我认为他们能够做到这一点的实际机制将会相当狭窄，而这可能是他们现在必须先向选民解释的事情。

paras.en: Leah Feiger: Absolutely. Hugo, how about you?
paras.zh: 利亚·费格：当然。雨果，你呢？

paras.en: Hugo Lowell: Yeah, just on the presidential question to Democrats, I think it's actually quite a wide-open field and you'll have to see how the new dynamics and the new Congress play out. You do have these freshman Democrats who are going to come in very, very aggressive. And then you also have people like Ossoff who are going to be riding on a wave of a lot of goodwill and a lot of momentum inside the Democratic Party. I think what's more interesting is Republicans because this really screws up a lot of timelines for people, two front-runners that keep getting mentioned, obviously JD Vance as the vice president, and then Rubio to a lesser extent. So on JD, there was a lot of thinking inside Trump world that JD, if it was an OK night, could announce pretty soon after the midterms. He had his donors more or less lined up, but it strikes me that that is now actually going to have to be paused. There is no way a Republican candidate can announce anytime soon with the stench of these midterms coming off on their coattails. It's just not possible. It's just a terrible, terrible political environment for Republicans. And it may only get worse if Trump decides to be an open warfare with Democrats on the Hill, and if he decides to go harder against Iran, that actually conversely might hurt Republicans more. And so I think JD Vance now has a very nuanced and difficult decision as to when he's going to announce, if ever. And as for someone like Marco Rubio, I have always been of the belief, and this is just me talking to people in Rubio's orbit, that he was not particularly enthralled about running this cycle. He saw JD as the heir apparent. There were a lot of movements inside Trump law to make sure that JD got it. And now again, he has a difficult decision. If he decides to run, does he wait for JD to announce and then potentially flame out? Or does he wait and see if he just announces at the same time as JD? Or does he decide actually, JD's cooked and now is the time for him to announce, this is the moment for him and he should go right now? I mean, these are all questions that are really unanswerable. And my guess is actually everyone takes a step back, takes stock, see how the next maybe six, 12 months play out before they get going.
paras.zh: 雨果·洛厄尔：是的，就民主党的总统问题而言，我认为这实际上是一个非常开放的领域，你必须看看新的动态和新的国会如何发挥作用。确实有这些民主党新人，他们将非常非常激进。然后还有像奥索夫这样的人，他们将利用民主党内部的大量善意和动力。我认为更有趣的是共和党人，因为这确实打乱了人们的很多时间表，两位不断被提及的领跑者，显然是副总统 JD 万斯，然后是卢比奥（程度较小）。因此，关于京东，特朗普内部有很多想法，如果这是一个不错的夜晚，京东可能会在中期选举后很快宣布。他或多或少地让他的捐助者排队，但令我震惊的是，现在实际上必须暂停。共和党候选人不可能在中期选举的恶臭影响下很快宣布自己的决定。这是不可能的。对于共和党人来说，这只是一个非常非常糟糕的政治环境。如果特朗普决定与美国进行公开战争，情况可能只会变得更糟 国会山上的民主党人，如果他决定对伊朗采取更严厉的措施，实际上相反可能会更多地伤害共和党人。因此，我认为 JD 万斯现在对于何时宣布（如果有的话）做出了一个非常微妙且困难的决定。至于像马可·卢比奥这样的人，我一直相信，这只是我与卢比奥周围的人交谈，他对运行这个周期并不特别着迷。他将 JD 视为法定继承人。特朗普法律内部有很多动作，以确保京东得到它。现在，他又面临一个艰难的决定。如果他决定参选，是否会等京东宣布后就可能熄火？还是观望他是否只是与京东同时宣布？或者他实际上决定，JD已经熟了，现在是他宣布的时候了，这是他的时刻，他应该现在就走？我的意思是，这些都是真正无法回答的问题。我的猜测是，实际上每个人都会后退一步，进行盘点，看看接下来的 6、12 个月会如何，然后再开始行动。

paras.en: Leah Feiger: David, how about you? What do you think?
paras.zh: 利亚·费格：大卫，你呢？你怎么认为？

paras.en: David Gilbert: Are we definitely ruling out a third term for Donald Trump? Is that off the table? Because Steve Bannon's still talking about it. He's still working on possibilities.
paras.zh: 大卫·吉尔伯特：我们肯定排除唐纳德·特朗普第三个任期吗？那是不可能的吗？因为史蒂夫·班农仍在谈论它。他仍在研究各种可能性。

paras.en: Leah Feiger: I love that this is the area of the internet that you're still steeped in. Obviously the four of us, different areas.
paras.zh: Leah Feiger：我喜欢你仍然沉浸在互联网领域。显然我们四个人，不同的领域。

paras.en: David Gilbert: It's interesting to me because obviously Trump, there's been a split in his base for quite a while now and we're seeing diverge even more after the midterms. But I'd love to know from Hugo actually, how important now, or is it important now, is Trump's endorsement? Because obviously for a long time, Trump was seen as the kingmaker and whoever he endorsed would be the person who would get the nomination. Has that weakened now because of the midterms?
paras.zh: 大卫·吉尔伯特：这对我来说很有趣，因为显然特朗普，他的支持者已经分裂很长一段时间了，我们看到中期选举后分歧更大。但我实际上很想从雨果那里知道，特朗普的支持现在有多重要，或者现在重要吗？因为显然很长一段时间以来，特朗普都被视为造王者，无论他支持谁，都会获得提名。现在由于中期选举而减弱了吗？

paras.en: Hugo Lowell: I think for congressional candidates, it's weakened. If you're a senator, if you're a member of Congress who your election coming up in two years time, I think the threat from White House officials, a threat from the president is not going to sway you. And by the way, we are already seeing this start to happen. Seeing people like Lauren Boebert and Thomas Massie be like, "You know what? YOLO, this is going to be my last stint in Congress. I'm going to vote to release the Epstein files." And there was nothing Trump could do sticking Lauren Boebert in a situation room that could change her mind. I think though for the presidential, things are, again, more complicated because if you heard someone like JD, if you're someone like Rubio, do you want Trump's base to turn out for you? Yes. Can you disown them completely? I don't think it's that easy. You still need to pick up a coalition. You still have to put together this coalition of super MAGA voters who still like Trump and who will still vote for him. You can't just write off that section of the voting populace. You still have to bring those voters with you. And if you don't get Trump's endorsement or Trump endorses someone else, then you're absolutely not going to get those voters.
paras.zh: 雨果·洛厄尔：我认为对于国会候选人来说，它被削弱了。如果你是一名参议员，如果你是一名国会议员，你的选举将在两年后进行，我认为来自白宫官员、来自总统的威胁不会动摇你。顺便说一句，我们已经看到这种情况开始发生。看到像劳伦·博伯特和托马斯·马西这样的人会说，“你知道吗？YOLO，这将是我在国会的最后一次任职。我将投票决定公布爱泼斯坦的文件。”特朗普将劳伦·博伯特困在战情室里也无法改变她的想法。我认为，对于总统来说，事情再次变得更加复杂，因为如果你听到像 JD 这样的人，如果你是像卢比奥这样的人，你希望特朗普的支持者支持你吗？是的。你能和他们彻底断绝关系吗？我认为这并不容易。你仍然需要组建一个联盟。你仍然必须组建这个超级MAGA选民联盟，他们仍然喜欢特朗普并且仍然会投票给他。你不能仅仅注销这部分投票人口。你仍然必须带着这些选民一起去。如果你没有得到特朗普的支持或者特朗普支持其他人，那么你绝对不会得到这些选民。

paras.en: David Gilbert: It's a very tricky needle to tread that you have to be able to move away from the negative aspect of what Trump brings, but also bring in all those people, as you say, who will no matter what he does, will turn out from tens of millions of numbers, obviously.
paras.zh: 大卫·吉尔伯特：这是一个非常棘手的问题，你必须能够摆脱特朗普带来的负面影响，但也要引进所有那些人，正如你所说，无论他做什么，显然都会从数以千万计的数字中脱颖而出。

paras.en: Hugo Lowell: But I think what is notable though is this is clearly a voting coalition that is very fluid, and Trump could capture them in '24. He lost them this cycle, but there's nothing to suggest in 18 months time, who knows what the news cycle is like and where we are at, that they cannot be won over again. I think that's how Republicans are thinking when they kind of look forward to the '28 cycle and the primary season.
paras.zh: 雨果·洛厄尔：但我认为值得注意的是，这显然是一个非常不稳定的投票联盟，特朗普可能会在 24 年击败他们。他在这个周期中失去了他们，但没有任何迹象表明在 18 个月的时间里，谁知道新闻周期是什么样的，我们处于什么位置，他们不能再次被赢得。我认为这就是共和党人在期待 28 年周期和初选时的想法。

paras.en: Leah Feiger: Is it bad to say that I'm really excited for '28? Guys, this is going to be so fun.
paras.zh: Leah Feiger：说我对 28 年感到非常兴奋是不是很糟糕？伙计们，这会很有趣。

paras.en: Hugo Lowell: Well, I'll be retiring. It's been a long road for this Trump reporter.
paras.zh: 雨果·洛厄尔：好吧，我要退休了。对于这位特朗普记者来说，这是一条漫长的道路。

paras.en: Leah Feiger: Hugo, David, Tori, thank you so much for joining us today. This was great.
paras.zh: Leah Feiger：Hugo、David、Tori，非常感谢你们今天加入我们。这太棒了。

paras.en: Leah Feiger: That's our show for today. We'll link to all the stories we spoke about in the show notes. Adriana Tapia produced this episode. It was mixed by Pran Bandi, who's also our New York studio engineer. It was fact-checked by Matt Giles and Daniel Roman. Kate Osborn is our executive producer, and Katie Drummond is WIRED's global editorial director.
paras.zh: Leah Feiger：这就是我们今天的节目。我们将链接到我们在演出笔记中谈到的所有故事。阿德里安娜·塔皮亚 (Adriana Tapia) 制作了本集。它是由 Pran Bandi 混音的，他也是我们纽约工作室的工程师。马特·吉尔斯和丹尼尔·罗曼对此进行了事实核查。凯特·奥斯本 (Kate Osborn) 是我们的执行制片人，凯蒂·德拉蒙德 (Katie Drummond) 是《连线》的全球编辑总监。

articles.title: The 7 Best Early Black Friday TV Deals (2026)
articles.author: Harry Rabinowitz

paras.en: You should never buy a TV at full price. This is a hill I will die on, and I am proven right every year when I see 20-, 30-, and even 50-percent-off deals on some of the best TVs. Even though Black Friday is weeks away, I'm already seeing some great TV deals available now.
paras.zh: 您永远不应该以全价购买电视。这是一座我会死在上面的山，每年当我看到一些最好的电视有 20%、30%、甚至 50% 的折扣时，我就证明自己是对的。尽管距离黑色星期五还有几周时间，但我现在已经看到了一些很棒的电视优惠。

paras.en: If you're in the market for a new screen, now is a smart time to shop options of all sizes, from big, premium OLED TVs for a home theater to small art TVs for the bedroom. Because you'll be ahead of the deal-hunting masses, you probably won't have to worry about shipping delays or out-of-stock notifications. A WIRED reviewer has tried every TV featured below (with one exception, the LG C6, which is currently in testing).
paras.zh: 如果您正在市场上购买新屏幕，现在是购买各种尺寸选择的明智时机，从用于家庭影院的大型优质 OLED 电视到用于卧室的小型艺术电视。因为您将领先于寻找交易的大众，所以您可能不必担心发货延迟或缺货通知。一位《连线》评论者尝试了以下每一款电视（其中一个例外，目前正在测试的 LG C6）。

paras.en: For more great discounts, check out our Best Early Black Friday Deals, as well as early discounts on smart bird feeders, mattresses, and espresso machines.
paras.zh: 如需更多折扣，请查看我们的黑色星期五最佳早期优惠，以及智能喂鸟器、床垫和浓缩咖啡机的早期折扣。

paras.en: This is the lowest price I've ever seen for the 65-inch LG C6, a fantastic deal on an excellent OLED TV. LG's C-Series TVs are consistently among our top picks due to their high brightness, uniform blacks, and vivid, natural colors. Add in their ample connectivity, which makes them versatile enough for gamers, and it's clear why this is a top OLED pick.
paras.zh: 这是我所见过的 65 英寸 LG C6 的最低价格，对于一款出色的 OLED 电视来说，这是一笔非常划算的交易。 LG 的 C 系列电视因其高亮度、均匀的黑色以及生动、自然的色彩而一直是我们的首选。再加上其充足的连接性，这使得它们对于游戏玩家来说足够通用，这很明显为什么它是 OLED 的最佳选择。

paras.en: The premium 2026 Samsung S95H OLED TV is now at its lowest price yet. WIRED reviewer John Brandon praised the TV for its accurate color and deep blacks. New to the latest S95H model is a silver bezel that’s recessed behind the main OLED panel, making the TV look like a metal picture frame.
paras.zh: 2026 款优质三星 S95H OLED 电视目前处于迄今为止的最低价格。 《连线》评论家约翰·布兰登称赞该电视色彩准确，黑色深邃。最新 S95H 型号的新增功能是银色边框，凹入主 OLED 面板后面，使电视看起来像金属相框。

paras.en: I understand wanting a nice OLED TV but not wanting to pay premium OLED prices. That's where budget OLEDs like the LG B6 shine—especially when steeply discounted. The 48-inch version, in particular, is 50 percent off at Best Buy right now, which is such a good deal, I thought it was a typo. (I won’t be surprised if the price mysteriously goes up.) Brandon praised the TV's thin size, simple setup, and deep and rich blacks.
paras.zh: 我理解想要一台漂亮的 OLED 电视，但又不想支付高价 OLED 价格。这就是像 LG B6 这样的廉价 OLED 的亮点——尤其是在大幅折扣的情况下。特别是 48 英寸版本，现在百思买有 50% 的折扣，太划算了，我以为是打字错误。 （如果价格神秘上涨，我不会感到惊讶。）布兰登称赞电视的纤薄尺寸、简单的设置以及深沉而丰富的黑色。

paras.en: This isn’t a huge discount, and I wouldn’t be surprised if the price went down closer to Black Friday. Even so, the TCL QM6K is one of the best TVs for most people, according to former WIRED reviewer Ryan Waniata, because of its well-rounded picture and reasonable price (even when not on sale).
paras.zh: 这并不是一个很大的折扣，如果价格在接近黑色星期五时下降，我也不会感到惊讶。即便如此，根据前《连线》评论员 Ryan Waniata 的说法，TCL QM6K 仍然是大多数人最好的电视之一，因为它的画面全面且价格合理（即使不打折）。

paras.en: Again, this isn’t the biggest discount I’ve seen for this TV, but 33 percent off is nothing to sneeze at for an already good-value television. In his U7SG review, Waniata called this a near-premium model with a new-and-improved stand and an anti-reflective matte screen reminiscent of high-end Samsung models.
paras.zh: 再说一次，这并不是我见过的这款电视的最大折扣，但对于一台已经很超值的电视来说，33% 的折扣不容小觑。在他的 U7SG 评测中，Waniata 称这是一款近乎高端的机型，具有全新改进的支架和防反射磨砂屏幕，让人想起高端三星机型。

paras.en: The best art TV is Samsung's Frame Pro (2026) thanks to its excellent image quality, contrast, color depth, and anti-glare technology that far outshines competition, says Brandon. The only problem is that it's historically been high-priced. While 17 percent off may not sound that impressive, it’s actually matching the Prime Day low I saw earlier this year for the same model.
paras.zh: 布兰登表示，最好的艺术电视是三星的 Frame Pro (2026)，其出色的图像质量、对比度、色彩深度和防眩光技术远远超过了竞争对手。唯一的问题是它的历史价格很高。虽然 17% 的折扣听起来可能没有那么令人印象深刻，但实际上与我今年早些时候看到的同一型号的 Prime Day 最低价相当。

paras.en: This discount isn't as low as its Prime Day price (yet), but 50 percent off is still great and makes this budget-friendly art TV even more appealing—especially for secondary rooms. It's not as bright as Samsung's art TVs, but it does come with a far broader free art library, no subscription fee needed.
paras.zh: 此折扣虽然还没有 Prime Day 价格那么低，但 50% 的折扣仍然很棒，并使这款经济实惠的艺术电视更具吸引力，尤其是对于次要房间。它不像三星的艺术电视那么明亮，但它确实配备了更广泛的免费艺术库，无需订阅费。

articles.title: 6 Best VPN Services (2026), Tested and Reviewed
articles.author: Jacob Roach

paras.en: Hundreds of VPNs are at your disposal. They all want you to believe they’re the best VPN you can buy. All of them claim to have the biggest network or a no-logging policy. And they all promise your internet traffic is safe on the network of servers they’ve rented. Only some of them are telling the truth.
paras.zh: 数百个 VPN 可供您使用。他们都希望你相信他们是你能买到的最好的 VPN。他们都声称拥有最大的网络或无日志记录政策。他们都承诺您的互联网流量在他们租用的服务器网络上是安全的。只有其中一些人说的是实话。

paras.en: VPNs are only growing in popularity due to age-verification laws in the UK and in several states in the US. Even if you don’t want a VPN, you might need one. If you’re hesitant, I get it. VPN providers have been deep in murky waters for years, constantly caught lying about their practices, handing over user data that was never supposed to be logged, and serving as safe havens for large cybercriminal organizations.
paras.zh: 由于英国和美国几个州的年龄验证法，VPN 越来越受欢迎。即使您不需要 VPN，您也可能需要一个。如果你犹豫的话，我明白了。 VPN 提供商多年来一直深陷浑水，不断被发现对其做法撒谎、交出本来不应该被记录的用户数据，并成为大型网络犯罪组织的安全港。

paras.en: I wanted to find the VPN services that actually work; the ones that keep their promises even in the face of potential prosecution, and the ones that have a proven track record of reliable performance. Some of the picks in this guide aren’t conventional, and some of the services I suggest you avoid might be controversial. But these are the top VPNs I’d use day to day.
paras.zh: 我想找到真正有效的 VPN 服务；那些即使面临潜在起诉也能信守承诺的公司，以及那些拥有可靠业绩记录的公司。本指南中的一些选择并不传统，我建议您避免的一些服务可能会引起争议。但这些是我日常使用的顶级 VPN。

paras.en: Read our other VPN guides, including how to set up a VPN on your router and how to use a VPN to watch Netflix when you travel abroad.
paras.zh: 阅读我们的其他 VPN 指南，包括如何在路由器上设置 VPN 以及如何在出国旅行时使用 VPN 观看 Netflix。

paras.en: What Does a VPN Do? And How Does It Work?
paras.zh: VPN 有什么作用？它是如何运作的？

paras.en: VPN stands for virtual private network. A VPN provides a tunnel through which all of your internet traffic passes. Instead of connecting to your internet service provider's servers, you connect to a VPN's server before connecting to the broader internet. Because most VPN services operate this way, your browsing data isn't stored, essentially making you anonymous online.
paras.zh: VPN 代表虚拟专用网络。 VPN 提供了一条隧道，所有互联网流量都通过该隧道。您无需连接到互联网服务提供商的服务器，而是先连接到 VPN 的服务器，然后再连接到更广泛的互联网。由于大多数 VPN 服务都以这种方式运行，因此不会存储您的浏览数据，这实际上使您在网上处于匿名状态。

paras.en: The linchpin in this system is a VPN protocol. Today, nearly all internet traffic is encrypted, but that encryption happens only after you've established a connection with a website. A VPN protocol encrypts traffic before it reaches the VPN server, adding extra security on untrusted networks like public Wi-Fi at a coffee shop or airport. It doesn't help much on your personal network unless there is an intruder.
paras.zh: 该系统的关键是 VPN 协议。如今，几乎所有互联网流量都已加密，但只有在您与网站建立连接后才会进行加密。 VPN 协议会在流量到达 VPN 服务器之前对流量进行加密，从而为不受信任的网络（例如咖啡店或机场的公共 Wi-Fi）增加额外的安全性。除非有入侵者，否则它对您的个人网络没有多大帮助。

paras.en: By routing your traffic through a server in another location, you can also bypass geo-restrictions online, such as the content libraries available in different countries on Netflix or checking product availability in other regions of the world.
paras.zh: 通过将流量路由到另一个位置的服务器，您还可以在线绕过地理限制，例如 Netflix 上不同国家/地区提供的内容库或检查世界其他地区的产品可用性。

paras.en: VPNs can also be important when connecting to public Wi-Fi. If you're doing anything remotely sensitive on your computer at a coffee shop, a VPN is a good idea to protect your personal data.
paras.zh: 连接公共 Wi-Fi 时 VPN 也很重要。如果您在咖啡店的计算机上执行任何远程敏感操作，VPN 是保护您的个人数据的好主意。

paras.en: VPN prices vary widely, but most providers cost around $10 per month for a monthly plan. Pricing changes if you buy several months at once, and it gets even more complicated with full security suites, such as those offered by Nord Security and Proton.
paras.zh: VPN 价格差异很大，但大多数提供商的包月套餐费用约为每月 10 美元。如果您一次购买几个月，价格就会发生变化，而完整的安全套件（例如 Nord Security 和 Proton 提供的套件）会变得更加复杂。

paras.en: Most prominent VPN services offer multi-month or even multiyear discounts. These plans are often the best way to get your foot in the door, but some VPNs have recently faced class-action lawsuits over their auto-renewal practices. Although a handful of lawsuits have been filed, that doesn't mean these services necessarily engaged in illegal practices.
paras.zh: 大多数著名的 VPN 服务都提供数月甚至数年的折扣。这些计划通常是入门的最佳方式，但一些 VPN 最近因其自动续订做法而面临集体诉讼。尽管已经提起了一些诉讼，但这并不意味着这些服务一定从事非法行为。

paras.en: Free VPNs exist, as well, but you should avoid most of them. Some restrictive free plans from Proton and Windscribe are useful, but you should approach most free VPNs with skepticism.
paras.zh: 免费 VPN 也存在，但您应该避免其中的大多数。 Proton 和 Windscribe 的一些限制性免费计划很有用，但您应该对大多数免费 VPN 持怀疑态度。

paras.en: You'll come across a few of these terms in this guide as you generally shop for a VPN. Here's what they mean.
paras.zh: 当您通常购买 VPN 时，您会在本指南中遇到其中一些术语。这就是他们的意思。

paras.en: Double-hop: Connecting to two (or more) VPN servers in succession. This provides an extra layer of privacy if someone traces your network path, but it will vastly reduce speeds.
paras.zh: 双跳：连续连接到两个（或更多）VPN 服务器。如果有人跟踪您的网络路径，这会提供额外的隐私层，但会大大降低速度。

paras.en: Split tunneling: Allows you to choose which apps use the VPN tunnel. Useful if you want some apps (like your browser) to use the VPN tunnel but not others.
paras.zh: 分割隧道：允许您选择哪些应用程序使用 VPN 隧道。如果您希望某些应用程序（例如您的浏览器）使用 VPN 隧道而不是其他应用程序，则非常有用。

paras.en: Kill switch: A security feature in VPNs that will disable your internet connection if the VPN connection drops. A kill switch can prevent internet traffic from leaking if the VPN fails.
paras.zh: 终止开关：VPN 中的一项安全功能，如果 VPN 连接断开，它将禁用您的互联网连接。如果 VPN 出现故障，终止开关可以防止互联网流量泄漏。

paras.en: IP and domain block list: A list of IP addresses or domain names that are blocked inside the VPN tunnel. Some VPNs offer Domain Name System (DNS) blocking, too, which can block ads served from particular DNS servers.
paras.zh: IP 和域阻止列表：VPN 隧道内阻止的 IP 地址或域名列表。一些 VPN 还提供域名系统 (DNS) 阻止功能，这可以阻止特定 DNS 服务器提供的广告。

paras.en: Static IP: Most VPNs assign you a random IP address, or even rotate the IP address while you’re connected. If you need external access to your network with a network-wide VPN, you'll need a static IP address.
paras.zh: 静态 IP：大多数 VPN 会为您分配一个随机 IP 地址，甚至在您连接时轮换 IP 地址。如果您需要使用全网 VPN 从外部访问您的网络，则需要静态 IP 地址。

paras.en: Port forwarding: Allows you to forward a port on your private network, bypassing the VPN tunnel. Useful when you need external network access with a network-wide VPN, such as running a media server.
paras.zh: 端口转发：允许您绕过 VPN 隧道转发专用网络上的端口。当您需要使用全网 VPN 访问外部网络时非常有用，例如运行媒体服务器。

paras.en: NetShield: A feature specific to Proton VPN that blocks ads and trackers while connected to the VPN. Other services, such as Windscribe and NordVPN, offer similar features.
paras.zh: NetShield：Proton VPN 特有的功能，可在连接到 VPN 时阻止广告和跟踪器。其他服务，例如 Windscribe 和 NordVPN，也提供类似的功能。

paras.en: Dark web monitoring: A feature available in some VPNs, such as NordVPN and ProtonVPN, that will monitor the dark web for your email address or other personal information. You'll be notified if the information shows up on the dark web or as part of a breach.
paras.zh: 暗网监控：某些 VPN（例如 NordVPN 和 ProtonVPN）中提供的功能，可以监控暗网中您的电子邮件地址或其他个人信息。如果该信息出现在暗网上或作为违规行为的一部分，您将会收到通知。

paras.en: DAITA: A feature of Mullvad VPN that will introduce background noise to your connection, combating AI-assisted network analysis. Windscribe, NordVPN, and ProtonVPN offer similar features.
paras.zh: DAITA：Mullvad VPN 的一项功能，会在您的连接中引入背景噪音，对抗人工智能辅助的网络分析。 Windscribe、NordVPN 和 ProtonVPN 提供类似的功能。

paras.en: Short of a few exceptions, VPNs are legal around the world. That includes the US, UK, Canada, Australia, the EU, South Africa, and many countries in Central and South America. Places such as North Korea and Turkmenistan have VPN bans in place, but due to the extreme censorship in those countries, it's hard to verify what laws are on the books (and how they're enforced). You can probably guess the North Korean government's stance on bypassing censorship, though.
paras.zh: 除少数例外，VPN 在世界各地都是合法的。其中包括美国、英国、加拿大、澳大利亚、欧盟、南非以及中美洲和南美洲的许多国家。朝鲜和土库曼斯坦等地设有 VPN 禁令，但由于这些国家的严格审查制度，很难核实书面法律（以及如何执行）。不过，你或许可以猜到朝鲜政府对于绕过审查制度的立场。

paras.en: For everyone else, VPN legality only comes into play based on which VPN you use and what you use it for. Countries such as India and Russia call for compliance with the government, forcing providers like NordVPN to shut down servers in those regions. And, regardless of what country you're in, engaging in illegal activity while connected to a VPN is still illegal.
paras.zh: 对于其他人来说，VPN 合法性仅根据您使用的 VPN 及其用途而发挥作用。印度和俄罗斯等国家呼吁遵守政府规定，迫使 NordVPN 等提供商关闭这些地区的服务器。而且，无论您位于哪个国家/地区，连接到 VPN 时从事非法活动仍然是非法的。

paras.en: Update November 2026: We’ve added a mention of an early Black Friday deal for Proton VPN.
paras.zh: 2026 年 11 月更新：我们添加了 Proton VPN 早期黑色星期五优惠的提及。

paras.en: Surfshark: I've used Surfshark personally for a few years, and I'd still be using it if Proton didn't impress me so much. Surfshark is dead simple to use. It pops up and connects before swiftly getting out of my way so I can get on with my day. If you spring for a two-year plan, it's cheap. You can score over two years for around $54 with the Starter plan.
paras.zh: Surfshark：我个人已经使用 Surfshark 几年了，如果 Proton 没有给我留下太深刻的印象的话，我仍然会使用它。 Surfshark 使用起来非常简单。它会弹出并连接，然后迅速离开我，以便我可以继续我的一天。如果您选择两年计划，那么它很便宜。通过 Starter 计划，您只需 54 美元左右即可获得两年多的积分。

paras.en: If you want to dig in deeper, you can. Surfshark is one of the most feature-rich VPNs I've used, sporting the basics like a double-hop connection and split tunneling, as well as an ad blocker and email masking. Like Proton, Surfshark offers other security tools like antivirus and dark web monitoring if you pick up a more expensive plan. Surfshark loses out just a bit when it comes to privacy, however. It has a no-logs policy, and it maintains a transparency report and a warrant canary, so it’s not bad in this regard. However, it doesn't have open-source applications, so you’ll need a bit more faith in Surfshark’s app security than with some other VPN services.
paras.zh: 如果你想深入挖掘，也可以。 Surfshark 是我用过的功能最丰富的 VPN 之一，具有双跳连接和分割隧道等基本功能，以及广告拦截器和电子邮件屏蔽功能。与 Proton 一样，Surfshark 还提供其他安全工具，例如防病毒和暗网监控（如果您选择更昂贵的计划）。然而，Surfshark 在隐私方面略显逊色。它有无日志政策，并且维护透明度报告和权证金丝雀，因此在这方面还不错。然而，它没有开源应用程序，因此与其他一些 VPN 服务相比，您需要对 Surfshark 的应用程序安全性有更多的信心。

paras.en: EventVPN: This is a free, ad-supported VPN from ExpressVPN. Ads and VPNs don't really mix, but EventVPN says it's able to offer a free service via Apple's App Tracking Transparency (ATT) and Identifier for Advertisers (IDFA), basically allowing it to serve ads without harvesting your personal data. The problem is the pervasiveness of ads. A banner lives at the top of the app at all times, and you'll need to sit through a 30-second ad each time you connect or disconnect; a big problem when some servers post unreasonably slow speeds. I'll admit EventVPN is a unique concept, but I see nothing better than ProtonVPN or Windscribe for a free VPN service. And when it comes to the inconvenience of sitting through ads, it's straight-up worse.
paras.zh: EventVPN：这是 ExpressVPN 提供的免费且支持广告的 VPN。广告和 VPN 并没有真正混合在一起，但 EventVPN 表示，它能够通过苹果的应用程序跟踪透明度 (ATT) 和广告商标识符 (IDFA) 提供免费服务，基本上允许它在不收集您的个人数据的情况下提供广告服务。问题在于广告的普遍存在。横幅始终位于应用程序顶部，每次连接或断开连接时，您都需要观看 30 秒的广告；当某些服务器速度过慢时，这是一个大问题。我承认 EventVPN 是一个独特的概念，但我认为没有什么比 ProtonVPN 或 Windscribe 更好的免费 VPN 服务了。当谈到观看广告带来的不便时，情况就更糟了。

paras.en: IVPN: This privacy-focused VPN provider is similar to Mullvad. It does not ask you to create an account with a username, password, and email, but instead generates a random ID, which you use to log in. That helps preserve your anonymity, since that information can’t be tied to your usage even if IVPN suffered a security incident. IVPN also accepts cryptocurrency payments (Bitcoin and Monero). Unlike Mullvad, IVPN offers one-year, two-year, and three-year plan options, as well as an unusual weekly option, which might be nice if you want a VPN while on vacation (IVPN standard is $2 per week). These can be more affordable than Mullvad’s monthly fee. However, IVPN lacks some privacy features you will find with Mullvad, such as RAM-less servers. IVPN scheduled a security audit for 2025, but as of January 2026, the results have not been posted. IVPN also has a tight two-device limit on the Standard plan. The Pro plan raises that to seven, but the Pro plan’s price is $10 per month, so it’s more expensive than Mullvad, which has a five-device limit. That remains true even if you go with a multi-year IVPN plan. Still, IVPN is a fine alternative if you want annual plan options. And while most VPN apps serve their purpose, I do think IVPN’s app is both more attractive and easier to use than Mullvad’s. —Matthew S. Smith
paras.zh: IVPN：这个注重隐私的 VPN 提供商与 Mulvad 类似。它不会要求您使用用户名、密码和电子邮件创建帐户，而是生成一个随机 ID，您可以用它来登录。这有助于保护您的匿名性，因为即使 IVPN 遭受安全事件，该信息也无法与您的使用情况联系起来。 IVPN 还接受加密货币付款（比特币和门罗币）。与 Mulvad 不同，IVPN 提供一年、两年和三年计划选项，以及一个不寻常的每周选项，如果您想在度假期间使用 VPN，这可能会很好（IVPN 标准为每周 2 美元）。这些可能比 Mulvad 的月费更实惠。然而，IVPN 缺乏 Mulvad 中的一些隐私功能，例如无 RAM 服务器。 IVPN 计划于 2025 年进行安全审核，但截至 2026 年 1 月，结果尚未公布。 IVPN 对标准套餐也有严格的两台设备限制。 Pro 计划将数量增加到 7 台，但 Pro 计划的价格为每月 10 美元，因此它比 Mulvad 更贵，后者有 5 台设备的限制。即使您选择多年 IVPN 计划，情况仍然如此。不过，如果您需要年度套餐选项，IVPN 是一个不错的选择。虽然大多数 VPN 应用程序都能达到其目的，但我确实认为 IVPN 的应用程序比 Mulvad 的应用程序更具吸引力且更易于使用。 ——马修·S·史密斯

paras.en: Private Internet Access (PIA): With its long history in the VPN space, PIA has maintained a track record of defending user privacy—even in the face of actual criminal activity. In 2016, a criminal complaint was filed in Florida against Preston Alexander McWaters for threats made online. McWaters was eventually convicted and sentenced to 42 months in prison. Investigators traced the online threats back to PIA's servers and subpoenaed the company. As the complaint reads, “A subpoena was sent to [Private Internet Access], and the only information they could provide is that the cluster of IP addresses being used was from the east coast of the United States.” According to the complaint, McWaters engaged in several other identifying activities, but PIA wasn't among them. Despite such a clear view of a VPN provider upholding its no-logging policy, PIA didn't impress me during my tests. It delivered the worst speeds out of any VPN I tested, with more than a 50 percent drop on the closest US server. (Windscribe, for context, only dropped 15.6 percent of my speed.)
paras.zh: 私人互联网接入 (PIA)：PIA 在 VPN 领域拥有悠久的历史，即使面对实际的犯罪活动，PIA 也一直保持着保护用户隐私的记录。 2016 年，佛罗里达州因网上威胁对普雷斯顿·亚历山大·麦克沃特斯 (Preston Alexander McWaters) 提起刑事诉讼。麦克沃特斯最终被定罪并被判处 42 个月监禁。调查人员将在线威胁追溯到 PIA 的服务器，并传唤了该公司。正如投诉中所述，“传票已发送至 [Private Internet Access]，他们能提供的唯一信息是所使用的 IP 地址群来自美国东海岸。”根据诉状，麦克沃特斯还参与了其他几项身份识别活动，但 PIA 并不在其中。尽管 VPN 提供商坚持其无日志政策的观点如此清晰，但 PIA 在我的测试中并没有给我留下深刻的印象。它的速度是我测试过的所有 VPN 中最差的，在最近的美国服务器上速度下降了 50% 以上。 （Windscribe，为了上下文，我的速度只下降了 15.6%。）

paras.en: MysteriumVPN: This is the go-to dVPN, or decentralized VPN, as far as I can tell. The concept of a decentralized VPN has existed for a while, but it's really gained traction over the last couple of years. The idea is to have a network of residential IP addresses that make up the network, routing your traffic through normal IP addresses to get around the increasingly common block lists for VPN servers. Mysterium accomplishes this network with MystNodes. It's a crypto node. People buy the node to earn crypto, and they're put into the Mysterium network. It's not inherently bad, but routing your traffic through a single residential IP is a little worrisome. Even without the decentralized kick, Mysterium was slow, and it doesn't maintain any sort of privacy materials, be it a third-party audit, warranty canary, or transparency report.
paras.zh: MysteriumVPN：据我所知，这是首选 dVPN，即去中心化 VPN。去中心化 VPN 的概念已经存在了一段时间，但它在过去几年才真正受到关注。这个想法是建立一个由住宅 IP 地址组成的网络，通过普通 IP 地址路由您的流量，以绕过 VPN 服务器日益常见的阻止列表。 Mysterium 通过 MystNodes 完成了这个网络。这是一个加密节点。人们购买节点来赚取加密货币，然后将其放入 Mysterium 网络。这本质上并不是坏事，但通过单个住宅 IP 路由流量有点令人担忧。即使没有去中心化的支持，Mysterium 的速度也很慢，而且它不维护任何类型的隐私材料，无论是第三方审计、保修金丝雀还是透明度报告。

paras.en: PrivadoVPN: A popular option to recommend as a free VPN, offering a decent free service, with a handful of full-speed servers and 10 GB of data per month. You'll have to suffer through four—yes, four—redirects begging you to pay for a subscription before signing up, but the free plan works. The problem is how new PrivadoVPN is. There's no transparency report or audit available, and although the speeds are decent, they aren't as good as Proton, Windscribe, or Surfshark. PrivadoVPN isn't bad, but it's hard to recommend when Proton and Windscribe exist with free plans that are equally as good.
paras.zh: PrivadoVPN：作为免费 VPN 推荐的流行选项，提供不错的免费服务，拥有少量全速服务器和每月 10 GB 数据。在注册之前，您将不得不经历四次（是的，四次）重定向，恳求您支付订阅费用，但免费计划有效。问题是 PrivadoVPN 有多新。没有可用的透明度报告或审计，尽管速度不错，但它们不如 Proton、Windscribe 或 Surfshark。 PrivadoVPN 还不错，但当 Proton 和 Windscribe 都提供同样好的免费套餐时，就很难推荐了。

paras.en: You'll find dozens of free VPNs all claiming to protect your privacy. Most of them don't. There are plenty of VPNs I don’t recommend, but these are a few I've tested that are worth mentioning.
paras.zh: 您会发现数十个免费 VPN 都声称可以保护您的隐私。他们中的大多数人都没有。有很多VPN我不推荐，但这些是我测试过的一些值得一提的VPN。

paras.en: X-VPN is available on desktop, but it primarily shows up in results on the Apple App Store and Google Play, targeting mobile users with a free offering. X-VPN hasn't done anything explicitly wrong like Hola, but it has way too many inconsistencies to recommend. For starters, it uses a proprietary VPN protocol, which it obfuscates within the app. Proprietary protocols like NordVPN's NordLynx and ExpressVPN's Lightway are based on existing, open-source protocols. Further, X-VPN was highlighted in a Tech Transparency Project report about free VPNs with links to the Chinese government; X-VPN is based in Hong Kong. There's no smoking gun with X-VPN, but there doesn't need to be. The speeds aren't the best, the app lacks basic features like split tunneling, and the pricing for a paid plan is in line with top providers.
paras.zh: X-VPN 可在桌面上使用，但它主要出现在 Apple App Store 和 Google Play 的搜索结果中，针对移动用户提供免费服务。 X-VPN 并没有像 Hola 那样做任何明显错误的事情，但它有太多不一致之处，不值得推荐。首先，它使用专有的 VPN 协议，并在应用程序中对其进行混淆。 NordVPN 的 NordLynx 和 ExpressVPN 的 Lightway 等专有协议基于现有的开源协议。此外，X-VPN 在一份关于免费 VPN 的技术透明度项目报告中得到了强调，并附有中国政府的链接； X-VPN 总部位于香港。 X-VPN 没有确凿证据，但也没有必要。速度不是最好的，该应用程序缺乏诸如分割隧道之类的基本功能，并且付费计划的定价与顶级提供商一致。

paras.en: Functionally, a VPN should do two things: keep your internet speed reasonably fast, and actually protect your browsing data. That's where I focused my testing. Extra features, a comfy UI, and customization settings are great, but they don't matter if the core service is broken.
paras.zh: 从功能上讲，VPN 应该做两件事：保持您的互联网速度相当快，并真正保护您的浏览数据。这就是我集中测试的地方。额外的功能、舒适的用户界面和自定义设置都很棒，但如果核心服务被破坏，它们就无关紧要了。

paras.en: Speed testing requires spot-checking, as the time of day, the network you're connected to, and the specific VPN server you're using can all influence speeds. Because of that, I always set a baseline speed on my unprotected connection directly before recording results, and I ran the test three times across both US and UK servers. With those baseline drops, I spot-checked at different times of the day over the course of a week to see if the speed decrease was similar.
paras.zh: 速度测试需要抽查，因为一天中的时间、您连接的网络以及您使用的特定 VPN 服务器都会影响速度。因此，我总是在记录结果之前直接在未受保护的连接上设置基准速度，并且在美国和英国服务器上运行了三次测试。对于这些基线下降，我在一周内每天的不同时间进行抽查，看看速度下降是否相似。

paras.en: Security is a bit more involved. For starters, I checked for DNS, WebRTC, and IP leaks every time I connected to a server using Browser Leaks. I also ran brief tests sniffing my connection with Wireshark to ensure all of the packets being sent were secured with the VPN protocol in use.
paras.zh: 安全性涉及更多一些。首先，我每次使用浏览器泄漏连接到服务器时都会检查 DNS、WebRTC 和 IP 泄漏。我还进行了简短的测试，嗅探我与 Wireshark 的连接，以确保发送的所有数据包都受到所使用的 VPN 协议的保护。

paras.en: On the privacy front, the top-recommended services included on this list have been independently audited, and they all maintain some sort of transparency report. In most cases, there's a proper report, but in others, such as Windscribe, that transparency is exposed through legal proceedings.
paras.zh: 在隐私方面，此列表中最推荐的服务都经过独立审核，并且它们都保留某种透明度报告。在大多数情况下，都会有适当的报告，但在其他情况下，例如 Windscribe，透明度是通过法律程序公开的。

articles.title: Gunman kills 8 in western Turkey shooting spree

paras.en: Nov. 6 (UPI) -- Turkish authorities have arrested a gunman accused of killing eight people and seriously injuring another in a series of shootings in western Turkey.
paras.zh: 11月6日（UPI）——土耳其当局逮捕了一名枪手，他被控在土耳其西部发生一系列枪击事件，造成八人死亡、一人重伤。

paras.en: The suspect was apprehended alive in Eskisehir province during a joint operation by provincial police and gendarmerie officers, the Eskisehir Governor's Office said in a statement.
paras.zh: 埃斯基谢希尔省省长办公室在一份声明中称，该嫌疑人在埃斯基谢希尔省警察和宪兵的联合行动中被活捉。

paras.en: The shootings occurred Thursday at several locations in western Turkey's Afyonkarahisar province, including central Afyonkarahisar, Ihsaniye district and the town of Anitkaya, the Afyonkarahisar Chief Public Prosecutor's Office said in a statement.
paras.zh: 阿菲永卡拉希萨尔首席检察官办公室在一份声明中表示，周四，土耳其西部阿菲永卡拉希萨尔省的多个地点发生了枪击事件，包括阿菲永卡拉希萨尔中部、伊萨尼耶区和阿尼特卡亚镇。

paras.en: The prosecutor's office said it had launched an investigation, assigning a deputy chief public prosecutor and three public prosecutors to the case.
paras.zh: 检察机关表示，已立案调查，并指派一名副检察长和三名检察官负责此案。

paras.en: Two victims killed were identified in a social media statement from Afyonkarahisar provincial education director Ismail Altinkaynak as teachers at Yukaritandir Middle School.
paras.zh: 阿菲永卡拉希萨尔省教育主任伊斯梅尔·阿尔廷凯纳克在社交媒体声明中确认两名遇难者是尤卡里坦迪尔中学的教师。

paras.en: "To shed light on all aspects of the incident and ensure that the process is carried out properly, all relevant state institutions have been working in coordination since the initial moments of the attacks and are diligently continuing the necessary investigations," the Afyonkarahisar Governor's Office said in a statement.
paras.zh: 阿菲永卡拉希萨尔省长办公室在一份声明中表示：“为了查明事件的各个方面并确保进程正确进行，所有相关国家机构从袭击发生之初就一直在协调工作，并正在努力继续进行必要的调查。”

paras.en: "We pray for God's mercy upon those who lost their lives and extend our condolences and wishes for patience to their grieving families and loved ones."
paras.zh: “我们祈求上帝怜悯那些失去生命的人，并向他们悲伤的家人和亲人表示哀悼，并希望他们保持耐心。”

articles.title: Lucas Leach: 'Drummer Boy' Ben finds freedom, purpose in music

paras.en: NEW YORK, Nov. 6 (UPI) -- Lucas Leach says Benjamin Clem -- the unlikely hero he plays in the history-themed movie musical, Drummer Boy -- finds purpose and independence marching with the colonists during the American Revolution.
paras.zh: 纽约，11 月 6 日（合众国际社）——卢卡斯·利奇 (Lucas Leach) 表示，他在历史主题音乐剧《鼓手男孩》中扮演的看似不太可能的英雄本杰明·克莱姆 (Benjamin Clem) 在美国革命期间找到了与殖民者一起前进的目标和独立。

paras.en: "Freedom, for him, is the opportunity to be regarded as capable," Leach told UPI in a recent Zoom interview.
paras.zh: “对他来说，自由是被视为有能力的机会，”利奇在最近的 Zoom 采访中告诉合众国际社。

paras.en: "There's always a slight stigma against Ben [regarding] his ability to contribute to his family, to the town, to society, to the army," the actor said of Ben, whose injured leg tends to slow him down him.
paras.zh: “本（本）为家庭、城镇、社会、军队做出贡献的能力总是受到一些耻辱，”这位演员谈到本时说道，他受伤的腿往往会减慢他的速度。

paras.en: Iain Glen from Game of Thrones plays John Ambrose, the army major who hears Ben play the drum and knows his skills can be used to improve the morale of his men and communicate directions to soldiers in the field.
paras.zh: 《权力的游戏》中的伊恩·格伦扮演陆军少校约翰·安布罗斯，他听到本打鼓，知道他的技能可以用来提高部下的士气，并向战场上的士兵传达方向。

paras.en: "The war comes to Kingstown. The war comes home and he wants the opportunity to defend it as another soldier would, with guns, with violence. The pivotal moment in this film is where he realizes that he is unique. He has a talent. He has something so special, in a way, that can command a whole army," Leach said.
paras.zh: “战争来到了金斯敦。战争来到了家乡，他希望有机会像其他士兵一样，用枪、用暴力来保卫它。这部电影的关键时刻是他意识到自己是独一无二的。他有天赋。他有一些如此特别的东西，在某种程度上，可以指挥整个军队，”利奇说。

paras.en: "Ambrose makes him believe that his talent is one of the most important things out there and he gets the freedom to express himself," he added.
paras.zh: “安布罗斯让他相信他的才华是最重要的事情之一，他可以自由地表达自己，”他补充道。

paras.en: "He is a musically inclined boy and that's always been his gift and no one's even regarded as anything other than a little quirk he has. I think, given that freedom, when he's on that battlefield in that final scene... he can pull off something pretty unexpected."
paras.zh: “他是一个有音乐天赋的男孩，这一直是他的天赋，除了他的一个小怪癖之外，没有人认为他有任何其他东西。我认为，考虑到这种自由，当他在最后一幕的战场上时......他可以完成一些非常意想不到的事情。”

paras.en: Grammy-winning For King & Country singer Joel David Smallbone plays Benjamin's brother Jeremiah, who is fighting on the side of the British.
paras.zh: 格莱美奖得主《For King & Country》歌手乔尔·大卫·斯莫尔博恩 (Joel David Smallbone) 饰演本杰明的弟弟耶利米 (Jeremiah)，他在英国人一边战斗。

paras.en: One of the final scenes of the film shows Ben marching onto a field playing the iconic "Drummer Boy" song while the American soldiers face off against the British, including Jeremiah.
paras.zh: 影片的最后一幕是，本在演奏着标志性的“鼓手男孩”歌曲走上田野，而美国士兵则与包括耶利米在内的英国士兵对峙。

paras.en: "It was crazy and it was really scary. It's a massive, massive open field. Everyone's watching. It's an expensive thing," Leach recalled.
paras.zh: “这太疯狂了，真的很可怕。这是一个巨大的、巨大的开放场地。每个人都在看着。这是一件昂贵的事情，”利奇回忆道。

paras.en: "We had to get it right. It felt so real. So much of what you see in this film is real. There's practical effects," he added.
paras.zh: “我们必须把它做好。感觉很真实。你在这部电影中看到的很多东西都是真实的。有实际效果，”他补充道。

paras.en: "There's fake snow we've laid there and you feel the footprints, you feel the crunching of the snow beneath your feet as you're going out, rendering yourself the easiest target in the world, putting yourself in the middle of that field. It was intimidating."
paras.zh: “我们在那里铺了假雪，当你走出去时，你会感觉到脚印，感觉到脚下雪的嘎吱声，让自己成为世界上最容易的目标，把自己放在那片场地的中间。这太吓人了。”

paras.en: The moment that Ben and Jeremiah embraced was filmed several times from different angles.
paras.zh: 本和耶利米拥抱的那一刻被从不同的角度拍摄了好几次。

paras.en: "We had to keep going again and again and again. I could feel and hear the gun firing," Leach said.
paras.zh: “我们必须一次又一次地继续前进。我能感觉到并听到枪声，”利奇说。

paras.en: "I'd start to play relentlessly and be in that moment of a young man, as his whole life had people put themselves in front of him, so he's protected, and him coming out of the shadow in a way and sacrificing himself for his older brother," he added.
paras.zh: “我会开始坚持不懈地打球，处于一个年轻人的那个时刻，因为他的一生都有人把自己放在他面前，所以他受到保护，他以某种方式走出阴影，为他的哥哥牺牲自己，”他补充道。

paras.en: "A million bullets could fly, he wasn't going to stop there. So, the environment that we were in meant that that was able to happen and I felt so alive and, at the end of that day of filming, I called my parents thinking that was one of the best things I've probably done."
paras.zh: “一百万颗子弹可以飞翔，他不会停在那里。所以，我们所处的环境意味着这能够发生，我感觉自己充满活力，在那天拍摄结束时，我打电话给我的父母，认为这可能是我做过的最好的事情之一。”

paras.en: Smallbone also co-directed alongside his real-life brother Ben, while their sibling Luke served as a producer on the project.
paras.zh: 斯莫尔博恩还与他现实生活中的兄弟本共同执导，而他们的兄弟卢克则担任该项目的制片人。

paras.en: The film is set for theatrical release on Friday.
paras.zh: 这部电影定于周五在影院上映。

articles.title: British doctor infected with Ebola in DRC evacuated to London

paras.en: Nov. 6 (UPI) -- A British doctor who contracted Ebola while working in the Democratic Republic of the Congo has returned home to receive specialized treatment, Britain's Department of Health and Social Care said Thursday.
paras.zh: 11月6日（UPI）——英国卫生和社会保障部周四表示，一名在刚果民主共和国工作时感染埃博拉病毒的英国医生已返回家中接受专门治疗。

paras.en: The patient is receiving care in a high-level isolation unit at the Royal Free Hospital in London, the health department said, adding that the unit is highly specialized and specifically designed for such a purpose.
paras.zh: 卫生部门表示，该患者正在伦敦皇家自由医院的高级隔离病房接受护理，并补充说该病房高度专业化，专门为此目的而设计。

paras.en: "UKHSA and the NHS have well-established and robust infection prevention and control protocols to limit the risk of onward transmission," Dr. Renu Bindra, deputy director for All Hazards Public Health Response at UK Health Security Agency, said in a statement, adding that "the risk to the wider public remains low."
paras.zh: 英国卫生安全局所有危害公共卫生应对部门副主任雷努·宾德拉博士在一份声明中表示：“英国卫生安全局和国民医疗服务体系拥有完善且强有力的感染预防和控制方案，以限制进一步传播的风险。”他补充说，“广大公众面临的风险仍然很低。”

paras.en: Britain worked with the DRC government, as well as other international health partners, to return the doctor on a medical evacuation flight.
paras.zh: 英国与刚果民主共和国政府以及其他国际卫生合作伙伴合作，通过医疗后送航班将这名医生接回。

paras.en: "The journey followed established infection prevention and control procedures, which also apply to everyone involved in the individual's care," the Department of Health and Social Care said.
paras.zh: 卫生和社会保障部表示：“这次旅行遵循了既定的感染预防和控制程序，这些程序也适用于参与个人护理的每个人。”

paras.en: The evacuation comes as the DRC combats a growing outbreak of Ebola caused by the rare and severe Bundibugyo virus.
paras.zh: 此次撤离正值刚果民主共和国抗击由罕见且严重的本迪布焦病毒引起的日益严重的埃博拉疫情。

paras.en: The earliest suspected case was a healthcare worker in the DRC who developed symptoms in late April and subsequently died. The DRC government declared an outbreak on May 15.
paras.zh: 最早的疑似病例是刚果民主共和国的一名医护人员，他于四月下旬出现症状，随后死亡。刚果民主共和国政府于5月15日宣布疫情爆发。

paras.en: Since then, there have been more than 10,660 cases and 5,198 deaths in the DRC as of Tuesday, with infections also confirmed in Kenya, Nigeria and Uganda as well as France, according to the U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention.
paras.zh: 据美国疾病控制与预防中心称，截至周二，刚果民主共和国已有超过 10,660 例病例，5,198 人死亡，肯尼亚、尼日利亚、乌干达以及法国也确诊了感染病例。

paras.en: The British doctor who contracted Ebola amid the current outbreak is the first confirmed British case to be evacuated to Britain since it began. France's single case was a doctor who was returning from a humanitarian mission in late June.
paras.zh: 在当前疫情爆发期间感染埃博拉病毒的英国医生是自疫情爆发以来第一例被撤离到英国的英国确诊病例。法国的唯一病例是一名六月底从人道主义任务返回的医生。

paras.en: Uganda has declared itself Ebola-free after its last patient was released from care on July 16.
paras.zh: 乌干达在 7 月 16 日最后一名患者出院后宣布本国已消除埃博拉病毒。

paras.en: "I commend the authorities of the Democratic Republic of the Congo and the United Kingdom for their exemplary cooperation in facilitating the safe medical evacuation of a patient with #Ebola disease caused by Bundibugyo vires for specialized care," Mohamed Janabi, the World Health Organization's regional director for Africa, said in a social media statement.
paras.zh: 世界卫生组织非洲区域主任穆罕默德·贾纳比在社交媒体声明中表示：“我赞扬刚果民主共和国和英国当局在促进本迪布焦病毒引起的埃博拉病毒患者安全医疗后送以接受专门护理方面的堪称典范的合作。”

paras.en: "While the patient continues to receive treatment in the UK, the DRC health authorities remain fully vigilant. Contact tracing, surveillance and other public health measures are ongoing to monitor and contain any potential risk of further transmission."
